films.description:
Irma Thomas, a trailblazing figure in New Orleans music, revisits her gospel roots in a recording session that spans genres and generations.


At 83 years old, Thomas brings together a diverse group of musicians in New Orleans to create a gospel album that speaks to her life’s journey, legacy, and enduring faith. The film captures intimate moments from the recording process with a remarkable ensemble of collaborators: Brazilian legend Jorge Ben, Christian music superstar Lauren Daigle, indie folk singer Valerie June, and pillars of the New Orleans music culture Cyril and Ivan Neville, Charlie Gabriel, Trombone Shorty, and Big Chiefs Shaka Zulu and David Montana. 


Beyond the studio Thomas reflects on her incredible life story, from her early days as a teenage mother of four, trying to break into the music business in the Segregation era, to becoming a beloved musical matriarch and the center of a large blended family with her husband and manager of 50 years, Emile Jackson. A portrait of a legendary artist: it is a testament to resilience, love, and the enduring power of music.




Director bio:

A musician and filmmaker, Ben Chace makes music full of images and films rich with sound. He has worked in Jamaica, Cuba, New Orleans, Nashville and his work is inspired by his curiosity for history and the threads of culture which link disparate people across time and space. He was raised in Providence, Rhode Island and now lives in Paris.


Film Sponsored by Film New Orleans and Henderson Hutter Group.

events.name: Lunch & Learn: Mindfulness for Filmmakers
events.description:
Film sets demand long hours, early call times, constant problem-solving, standing on your feet, unpredictable meals, and the ability to stay focused and creative under pressure.


Drawing from his book Sadhana: A Modern Spiritual Routine for a Healthier, Happier Life, Mark Berger will share practical mindfulness, movement, breath, and spiritual practices that actors, directors, producers, and production crews can use before call time, between setups, during meal breaks, and after wrap. We’ll explore simple ways to manage stress and anxiety, maintain energy, support physical health, and avoid letting the demands of production take over your well-being.


Designed specifically for the realities of working in the film industry, this lunch-and-learn offers tools that can be practiced in five minutes or woven into your entire day on set.

events.name: South Pitch Narrative Competition
events.description:
Admission is free and open to the public.


South Pitch is a high-energy showcase of the distinctive stories and filmmaking talent emerging from the American South.


Now in its 16th season, South Pitch is one of the New Orleans Film Festival’s signature industry programs, connecting Southern filmmakers with the funding, mentorship, and industry access to help move ambitious projects forward. Each year, five documentary and five narrative teams take the stage for five minutes to pitch their works-in-progress before a panel of industry leaders, who provide feedback and award additional funding to selected projects.

-----

In preparation for the pitch, every participating team receives one-on-one pitch training, a minimum $1,500 grant, travel support, and All-Access passes to the New Orleans Film Festival. The industry panel selects a winner and runner-up in both the documentary and narrative categories for additional funding, while audience members get a voice of their own, awarding a $500 Audience Award in each category.



Pitchers include:

Gerard Clarke and Rashielle Clarke (Acworth, Georgia) - Landfall: An immigrant girl must survive until dawn as Hurricane Andrew claws her family’s home open.


Nana Kumi (Natchez, Mississippi) - Blood for Soil: A woman awakens in a remote town with no recollection of how she arrived. She races to escape before its obscured past consumes her.


Christian Meola (Austin, Texas) - Other Days: Four college guy friends shatter their group dynamic when they realize a deeper need to be closer to each other across three stories.


Nolam Plaas (New Orleans, Louisiana) and Louis Anania (New York) - pecan: Junie and his father, Kenny, attempt to live up to expectations of being men.


Ivan Rome (Columbus, Georgia) - Hallelujah Night: A pastor's kid and his two best friends sneak out for their first Halloween party.

Originally from Tegucigalpa, Honduras, Mariana Martinez is a peacebuilder and storyteller who is fiercely committed to telling stories from the Latin American diaspora.


Jess Daddio is a Virginia-born-and-raised filmmaker with a soft spot for stories from the South. She produced the Patagonia-backed short documentary "Monte: Can't Stop, Won't Stop." "¡Hola, Paisano!" is their directorial debut.

films.name: Between Here and Home
films.short_description: This doc follows the sisters behind-the-scenes of their creative collaboration on the award-winning feature film "Take Me Home."
films.description:
Liz and Anna Sargent have a lot of questions about what the future holds for their family: the world beyond their home is not made for someone like Anna, who lives with a cognitive disability. Their answer? To make a movie. This short documentary follows the sisters behind-the-scenes of their creative collaboration on the award-winning feature film "Take Me Home," revealing how seeking answers in creative ways can lead to surprising outcomes.


Director bio:

Nathan Willis is an award-winning documentary filmmaker and lifelong Southerner whose work explores people, place, faith, disability, and the healing power of art. His films have screened at Tribeca Film Festival, DOC NYC, Slamdance, Big Sky Documentary Film Festival and The New Orleans Film Festival.

films.name: The Oldest Person in the World
films.short_description: A decade-long global odyssey chronicles the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.
films.description:
A Sundance favorite that turns an obsession with extreme longevity into a funny, moving meditation on what makes a life worth living.


Over the course of a decade, filmmaker Sam Green travels the world meeting the ever-changing record holders for the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of extraordinary longevity becomes something much more personal, as Green confronts the passage of time, mortality, and major changes in his own life. An intimate, often surprising celebration of aging, connection, and the simple wonder of being alive.


Director bio:

Sam Green is a NY-based documentary filmmaker. "The Oldest Person in the World" marks his seventh feature documentary at the Sundance Film Festival. His most recent film, "32 Sounds" (Oscar Shortlist), played opening night of both the 2022 Sundance and SXSW festivals. Sam’s 2004 feature-length film, "The Weather Underground," premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and was nominated for an Academy Award.

films.name: Zenón and the Rebel Boats
films.short_description: A biographical documentary about the life of fisherman, Carlos "Taso" Zenón who led the fishermen movement in Vieques to halt US Navy war games in the Caribbean Sea.
films.description:
An essential rediscovery of a Puerto Rican revolutionary and environmental hero in this Blackstar Film Festival Jury Winner.


Through never-before-seen archival footage, Juan Carlos Dávila Santiago chronicles the life and activism of Puerto Rican fisherman and revolutionary Carlos “Taso” Zenón, who spent decades organizing and fighting against the US military occupation of the island of Vieques, Puerto Rico. "Zenón and the Rebel Boats" transports the audience to Vieques to witness an unsung hero in a landmark environmental and anti-militarist campaign in the Caribbean. -JDOM



Director bio:

Born and raised in the westside of Puerto Rico, Juan C. Dávila Santiago is a documentary filmmaker, TV producer, and multi-media journalist. For more than 10 years, Dávila Santiago has reported and produced films about the colonial experience in Puerto Rico, focusing on environmental conflicts, social movements, and workers struggles.

films.name: Three Times (Tres Tiempos)
films.short_description: In a house between the mountains, facing a mirrored lake, Emma and her teenage granddaughter Alicia live together. Emma instills her passion for dance and raises Alicia as a mother, but Alicia falls prey to her controlling upbringing. The unexpected arrival of Barbara, Alicia’s mother and Emma’s daughter, accompanied by her caregiver, disrupts the routine of their small world.
films.description:
An enigmatic, dance-driven portrait of three generations of women, set against the wild beauty of southern Argentina—for fans of sumptuous international cinema. 


On the banks of a freshwater Patagonian lake, Alicia and her grandmother fill their days of solitude with a curious study of dance that centers feeling over conventional form. When their serenity is interrupted by the return of Alicia’s mother who suffers an unnamed disease that leaves her non-verbal and childlike, the balance of their duality shifts to a mystic trio. The mysterious landscape of their secluded home begins to unveil its secrets as the three women seek to find balance and trust between each other once again. -LD



Director bio:

Marlene Grinberg is an Argentine director and screenwriter. She has been working in the film industry since 2012. Her short films include "Mi reina" (Punta del Este Film Festival), "Hoy empieza otra vez" (Bafici, La mujer y el cine) and "Todas mis Lolas" (Marché du film, Primeiro Plano Brasil). She also co-directed the documentary "Me gusta cuando hablas" (Fidba). "Three Times (Tres tiempos)" is her debut feature film.

Cami Kwan is a queer Chinese-American director specializing in stop motion animation. She draws on her lived experience to create stories for young audiences that explore emotions, relationships, identity and culture. Kwan began her career on the Emmy-winning preschool series Tumble Leaf before joining forces with her business partners to found their independent animation studio, Apartment D.

films.short_description: Seeking answers in popular rituals, Adela feels that something is watching and harming her, and only religion seems to understand her. During a visit to a healer, she confesses the disturbing origin of her suffering.
films.description:

Director bio:

Bea Lema, b. 1985, A Coruña, Spain, is an illustrator and comic book author. Her work is generally autobiographical in nature, dealing with themes related to madness, trauma, family relationships, religion, and popular rituals. Graphically, she explores drawing and embroidery as mediums for her illustrations and comics.

Laurence has collaborated as a creative director with the National Film Board of Canada (NFB) and the Festival International du Film sur l’Art (FIFA).

Bianca Lambert is a filmmaker, journalist, and creative producer whose work explores storytelling, beauty, and Black women's experiences. Her short "Super High: A Period Piece" has won six awards and screened at Slamdance, Atlanta, and Chicago Film Festivals. Her second short, "My Black Is Cracking," is on the festival circuit this year. Her writing has appeared in ESSENCE, PEOPLE, and HuffPost.

Leto Stojanovic Meade is a UK animation director whose internationally acclaimed films have won awards at Oscar-, BAFTA-, and BIFA-qualifying festivals.


Jonathan Rockefeller is a writer, director, and producer of stage and screen whose honors include two New York Times Critics’ Picks and multiple Drama Desk and BroadwayWorld Awards, including Best Direction, Best New Play, and Best New Musical.

Playdoh Kolo is a New Orleans-based puppeteer, filmmaker, and interdisciplinary artist whose work combines puppetry, found objects, performance, and film. Their films explore surreal and ritualistic worlds through practical effects and handcrafted imagery, drawing on traditions of experimental theater and puppetry.

films.name: Paradaïz
films.short_description: Welcome to a place where the houses have holes, tomatoes are ticking time bombs and snails wander the streets in search of a safe space. Absurdist animation, archival images and slippery childhood memories combine to explore the real meaning of home.
films.description:
Welcome to a place where the houses have holes, tomatoes are ticking time bombs and snails wander the streets in search of a safe space. Sarajevo-born artist Matea Radic uses absurdist animation, archival images and her own slippery childhood memories to explore the real meaning of home.


Director bio:

Matea Radic is a multidisciplinary artist born in Sarajevo and based in Winnipeg, Canada. She fled her birthplace as a child in the summer of 1992 and has been interested in the concept of home and attachment ever since, infusing her art with a signature mix of nostalgia and dark humor.

films.short_description: In the face of her body fading into stardust, Shari realizes what truly matters to her.
films.description:

Kiana Naghshineh is a German-Iranian director from Mannheim. During her studies at the Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg, she created several award-winning films and was nominated for the Student Academy Award, the Student BAFTA, and the Annie Award. As a freelancer, she works as an animation director and designer.

films.name: Tell Me When You Get Home
films.short_description: During a family party, fifteen year-old Honest Cardamom encounters the spirit of an ancestor, reconnecting the teen to her own origin story.
films.description:
Fifteen-year-old Honest Cardamom hasn’t seen her mother since she was four, but at a crowded family party, she begins to feel her presence in ways she can’t explain. When Honest senses the presence of her mother, she finds the courage to ask her uncle about the woman she barely remembers and, in doing so, begins to uncover pieces of herself.


Director bio:

Tshay is a filmmaker and artist from Amityville, NY. She is a writer, director, producer, shooter, and editor whose work is an expansive case for optimism, play, and interiority. Working in close collaboration with loved ones, Tshay creates films across documentary, fiction and hybrid forms.

A story of entanglements between humans and mushrooms; the visible and invisible; generational knowledge and modern science.
films.description:
Prepare to see the natural world – and mushrooms – in a whole new way in this stunning SXSW award winner.


With one foot in ancestral knowledge and the other in modern science, two Indigenous mycologists traverse Mexico’s forests on a quest to better understand the interconnected existence of humans and fungi. This immersive journey invites the viewer to listen to and learn from the wisdom in the mushrooms all around us. -JDOM



Director bio:

Otilia Portillo Padua is a Mexican director who studied architecture at the University of Cambridge and the Architectural Association in London. Her films include "Three Voices" which premiered at SXSW, and the short documentary "Birders" for Netflix. She has received support from FONCA, IMCINE, the Sundance Institute, the Redford Center, Artist Accelerator, and Doc Society.


Film Sponsored by Roger Thayer Stone Center for Latin American Studies

films.name: You Don't Know My Name
films.short_description: Separated from his incarcerated mother at birth, the filmmaker searches for her identity. As he gets closer to this life-altering truth, he navigates his way through systems designed to keep him in the dark.
films.description:
A powerful and personal story of family and separation, that starts and ends in south Louisiana.


In 1984 Louisiana, filmmaker Tommy Franklin was separated from his mother at birth in prison and entered the foster system. In this astonishing, uncompromising feature debut, Tommy embarks on a fearless quest in search of his mom, as he confronts generational trauma and interrogates the fractures of state-enforced separation. "You Don't Know My Name" is formally inventive, fusing intimate verité, narrative sequences and performance art to bring deep symbolism to the filmmaker’s stirring journey of self discovery and collective healing. -AT


Director bio:

Tommy Franklin is a filmmaker, writer, and producer. He has received support from Sundance Institute, Film Independent, ITVS, Firelight Media, Ford Foundation/JustFilms, Catapult Film Fund, Perspective Fund, The Just Trust, BAVC Media, and many others. Franklin’s one hour drama pilot Intrepid was a finalist for 2021’s Sundance Episodic Lab. He was a 2022 Sundance BIPOC Mentorship Program Mentee.

films.name: White Lightning
films.short_description: A gritty, funny, and uniquely Southern story about second chances, legacy, and what it takes to outrun your past. This documentary follows the rise and fall of underground track legend Casey Combest (aka White Lightning) and his son King’s effort to break his father’s 25-year-old national high school record.
films.description:
A wildly charming slice of Kentucky Americana full of big personalities, fur coats, cases of Mountain Dew—and the irresistible spirit of a great sports movie. World Premiere.


In 1999, Casey Combest set the US High School Sprint Record for the 60 meter dash by completing it in 6.57 seconds. Today, his son King attempts to fulfill his father’s legacy and break his long-standing record. "White Lightning" traces the journey of a rising star whose career ended too soon, and the son who is trying to keep his father’s dreams alive and make his family proud. -JDOM



Director bio:

A veteran magazine journalist, Mark Anders got his start in film by happenstance in 2011 while on assignment for National Geographic in the Congo. After being invited to pen a feature documentary about that expedition, he was hooked. Mark has since served as a writer and producer on a handful of documentary features. "White Lightning" is his feature directorial debut.

films.name: Unseen Olympiad
films.short_description: "Unseen Olympiad" is a transcendental look at competing athletes from over 100 countries on the brink of greatness, telling a poetic story of unification through the universal emotional journey of sport.
films.description:
Experience the World Premiere of this 35mm print at the Prytania Theatre—an artful take on the spectacle of international sports.


Shot on impressionistic 16mm at the 2023 FISU World University Games in China and the United States, Unseen Olympiad looks beyond the spectacle of international competition to capture the embodied and emotional experiences of athletes. Across summer and winter sports, over 6,000 young competitors collectively experience anticipation, anxiety, exhaustion, focus, failure, and triumph. Statistics, national narratives, and the conventions of televised sports fall away to reveal an intimate, stirring, and unforgettable portrait of human endurance. -RLW



Director bio:

Casey Shaw is a filmmaker and mixed-media artist from the Southern United States. Casey's work in the non-fiction and documentary space revolves around archiving cultural moments on analog media to fight the evaporation and commercialization of authentic human connection. “Unseen Olympiad” is Casey’s first feature film and it was included in the Cultural Olympiad of the 2026 Winter Olympics.

films.name: Junkie
films.short_description: A meth-addicted mom embarks on an odyssey through the underbelly of the South in an attempt to evade rehab and redeem herself in the eyes of her son.
films.description:
A raw, wildly unpredictable portrait of addiction and recovery, starring a real-life survivor who helped shape the story from her own journals. From executive producer Patty Jenkins.


Perpetual screwup Stevie (Rocky Shay) is running on empty having just escaped from rehab [again]. On a quest to repay her debts and reconcile with her estranged, openly gay son, Liam, before skipping town for good, Stevie winds up in a slew of high-risk predicaments over the course of a few frenzied days. An unforgettable Southern odyssey, "Junkie" evolves into a touching, emotionally raw mother-and-son story about dignity, identity, and the fragile hope of redemption. 


Director bio:

William Means is a Los Angeles-based writer and director who earned his MFA in Directing at the AFI Conservatory. Since AFI, William has worked with Cinematographer Lawrence Sher as well as Director Patty Jenkins. His last short, "Blue Square Heart," qualified for the 2024 Oscars®. His debut feature, "Junkie," premiered at AFI Fest 2025.

films.name: More Than Bike Life
films.short_description: This film follows the rise of 1UP Bike Life through the eyes of four young riders whose commitment to the movement reflects something deeper than tricks or wheelies.
films.description:
It’s more than wheelies—it’s community and a way forward. “More Than Bike Life” captures the energy of New Orleans’ young riders, featuring music from La Reezy.


In a city known for its rhythm, resilience, and relentless challenges, a crew of young riders in New Orleans found purpose through pedals and pavement. What started as a local bike movement in New Orleans quickly became a lifeline—keeping kids out of trouble, off the streets, and locked into a culture of creativity and community. This film follows the rise of 1UP Bike Life through the eyes of four young riders whose commitment to the movement reflects something deeper than bike tricks—it’s about survival, legacy, and rewriting their story in a city that too often writes it for them.

As a director, he brings a unique understanding of action, performance, and camera to his work. His latest documentary, More Than Bike Life, explores New Orleans bike culture.

films.name: A Talent for Murder
films.short_description: A mysterious young man from a New York publisher is sent to Switzerland to persuade the renowned writer Patricia Highsmith to write one final installment of the Ripley anthology.
films.description:
A tour de force performance from the legendary Helen Mirren as irascible novelist Patricia Highsmith, author of The Talented Mr. Ripley, Carol, and other classic thrillers. 


An ambitious young New York publisher (Tony Award winner Alden Ehrenreich) travels to remote Switzerland to persuade the reclusive, eccentric writer Patricia Highsmith (Academy Award winner Helen Mirren) to write one final installment of her world-famous Ripley anthology. As the pair seek to bring one of literature’s most unforgettable sociopaths back to life, a mysterious woman (Olivia Cooke, “House of the Dragon”) appears in town, and life and fiction begin to blur. Director Anton Corbijn crafts a delicious, twisted thriller that both celebrates the undeniable legacy of Highsmith’s writing and interrogates the darkness that lies beneath the surface of high society. A Bleecker Street release. 


Director bio:

Anton Corbijn was born in Strijen, The Netherlands. He has made music videos for artists including David Bowie, Joy Division, Depeche Mode, and Nirvana. He directed the features "Control" (2007), which played the Festival, "The American" (2010), "A Most Wanted Man" (2010), and "Life" (2015). "A Talent for Murder" (2026) is his latest film.

At the 77th International Jugglers’ Association Festival in Green Bay, Wisconsin, Sonal, a fire dancer and stand-up comic, discovers she’s pregnant after a one-night stand with a mime. Meanwhile, Lucy, a cheeky street performer, navigates the balance between artistic satisfaction and financial security, while circus veteran Cyril attempts a risky new act to reignite his fading passion for the stage.

films.name: The Haunting of Pennhurst
films.short_description: For over 70 years, Pennhurst State School & Hospital was called a place of care. What happened inside killed over half its population. After closing in 1987, it left behind unmarked graves and an unresolved history. Today, on those same grounds, disabled performers prepare to scare visitors at the Pennhurst Asylum haunted attraction.
films.description:
Haunted-house thrills meet disability and the reclamation of a painful history. A Tribeca selection for Halloween fans, horror lovers, and disability advocates.


Do you believe in haunted gravesites? There is one filled with unmarked graves at Pennhurst State School and Hospital, which was finally shut down in 1987. Within it are unsolved cases of abuse and torture. These days, the people of Spring City, Pennsylvania, come to these haunted grounds to see the performers who have created an annual halloween spectacle. Many of these performers live with some of the same disabilities of those whose lives ended in this hospital. So as monsters, ghouls and zombies, they are able to reclaim and reap the profits, but not without confronting ideas around what it means to be a spectacle for entertainment, and how to do so on your own terms. -BT

films.description:

A layabout sound designer desperate to prove himself, Jim is working on a new horror flick from the tyrannical yet lauded b-movie director P.W. Griffin. Sent to the remote island where the film was shot to capture a sound powerful enough to elevate the film's finale, eerie local fables surface about missing youth and a ghostly sea captain recruiting a spectral crew. As Jim entangles himself further into the scenery, and prophecy, he can’t help but ponder the truth of the legend, and if recording it might just cost him more than his career.

films.description:

Like many women’s basketball stars, Brittney Griner went to Russia in search of greater financial opportunity. In 2022, her detention by Russian authorities sparked an international effort to secure her release, reaching the highest levels of power in Washington and Moscow. This gripping documentary chronicles Griner’s journey to Russia, the campaign to bring her home, and the renewed perspective she gained after returning to the United States.

films.short_description: When thousands of migratory birds descend upon an Iranian family’s citrus orchard, they face a difficult choice: protect the birds or protect the harvest that sustains their lives.
films.description:
Thousands of egrets, one orange grove, and one very divided family come together in this charming and unexpectedly funny Iranian tale of making room for the unexpected.


Sometimes families differ on what is a blessing, or a curse. In Jafar Sadeghi’s “Kabouk,” this notion takes the form of thousands of migrant egrets who descend upon the Golalipour family’s orange orchard. In the Iranian village of East Gaz, locals speculate on how Mr. Golalipour and his six sons are handling this invasion of Egrets on their orange farm. Beginning a routine of coming and going, to the sea and back over time, the family grows divided on methods of either getting rid of the Egrets, or embracing their presence. But can the orange trees survive them? The family has to make a living after all. Come along for a fascinating saga of a family trying to either save their orchard, or live a new life with a lively flock. -BT



Director bio:

Jafar Sadeghi is an independent Iranian documentary filmmaker known for socially engaged and thought-provoking films. With over a decade of experience, his works have been recognized at major festivals, including Fajr Film Festival and Cinema Vérité. His documentaries explore human stories and social issues.

films.name: Matininó
films.short_description: In Puerto Rico, a multi-generational group of women confront violence and abuse through a shared creative fantasy rich in color, mythology and play in this kaleidoscopic documentary.
films.description:
A deeply intimate act of collective storytelling, where a family turns the filmmaking process into a path toward healing. From a South Pitch alum.


Idaliz Villanueva has survived years of abuse in order to raise her two daughters safely. After multiple generations of women that experienced violence in their home, Villanueva brings the women and girls of her family together to create a film to confront and share their stories together. Director Gabriela Diaz Arp brings us along to witness their creative process: creating characters, building a world of memories they can return to, and reconciling with their pain. Through ancestral mysticism and the tradition of storytelling, these women discover a pragmatic way to share their collective trauma, and break the cycle once and for all. -BT



Director bio:

Gabriela Díaz Arp is an independent director and producer passionate about the ways visual language can deepen human understanding and connection. Her work challenges documentary conventions by incorporating fictional elements, new technologies, and pushing the boundaries of the form.

films.name: Whistle Down Wind
films.short_description: Across three chapters of childhood, adolescence, and adulthood, this film follows two girls from a happenstance meet cute to the drunken teenage kiss that propels their quirky friendship into a hidden love affair.
films.description:
A tender, bittersweet sapphic coming-of-age story steeped in the longing and contradictions of the rural South. 


When a drunken teenage kiss propels Janie and Alex’s quirky friendship into a hidden love affair, the conservative ideologies of their hometown force them to confront the truth about their sexualities, and the bitter future of their relationship. Andie Morgenlander's "Whistle Down Wind" is a tender, bittersweet sapphic coming-of-age story that explores the possibilities and limitations of queerness in the rural South, blending intimate character drama with the atmospheric textures of the Southern landscape.



Director bio:

Andie Morgenlander is dedicated to social change through cinematic storytelling. Their short films have screened nationally and internationally, known for intimate character explorations that often explore how we learn to love each other more fully. Their debut feature, "Whistle Down Wind" is on the festival circuit; notable acceptances include New Orleans Film Festival and Portland Film Fest.

films.name: Strangers on a Train
films.short_description: A charming psychopath tries to coerce a tennis star into his theory that two strangers can commit the perfect crime by exchanging murders—each killing the other’s most-hated person.
films.description:
Alongside our Spotlight screening of “A Talent for Murder,” NOFF revisits three classic Highsmith adaptations. Together, they offer a chance to revisit the cinematic legacy of one of the 20th century’s great psychological thriller writers. Additionally, the screenings of “Strangers on a Train” and “Purple Noon” come with a special introduction that dives into the science and psychology behind the characters and audience response to these thrillers. Supported by Science on Screen, an initiative of the Coolidge Corner Theatre, with major support from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation.


The film that started Patricia Highsmith’s extraordinary life on screen, and one of Alfred Hitchcock’s essential thrillers, “Strangers on a Train” follows tennis star Guy Haines after a chance meeting with the sinister Bruno Antony leads to a chilling proposition: they each kill the other’s enemy. What begins as a casual conversation soon becomes a deadly obsession, as Bruno refuses to let Guy walk away. With unforgettable set pieces and psychological tension, Hitchcock’s adaptation of Patricia Highsmith remains a landmark thriller.

events.name: Cinema Reset: Cyanotype Animation!
events.description:
This hands-on workshop combines the beautiful 19th century cyanotype photographic process with stop-motion animation. Using paper pre-coated with emulsion, we’ll arrange stencils, objects, and 16mm negatives, expose contact prints to sunlight, and process the images with water. They’ll then be scanned and incorporated into a collaborative animation which will be projected at the Independent Filmmaker Party on Monday night. You keep your cyanotype prints! 


All ages welcome (though children must be supervised by an adult), no experience necessary. Bring small items to create your own animated silhouettes!


Workshop Facilitated by Rachel Lynn Weaver and Tacie Jones


Cinema Reset is the NOFF expanded media showcase. Founded in 2011, the showcases groundbreaking projects at the intersections film, art, technology, and performance. We also offer workshops to share unique creative resources with the New Orleans community. Cinema Reset is curated by Rachel Lin Weaver.

events.name: South Pitch Documentary Competition
events.description:
Admission is free and open to the public.


South Pitch is a high-energy showcase of the distinctive stories and filmmaking talent emerging from the American South.


Now in its 16th season, South Pitch is one of the New Orleans Film Festival’s signature industry programs, connecting Southern filmmakers with the funding, mentorship, and industry access to help move ambitious projects forward. Each year, five documentary and five narrative teams take the stage for five minutes to pitch their works-in-progress before a panel of industry leaders, who provide feedback and award additional funding to selected projects.

-----

In preparation for the pitch, every participating team receives one-on-one pitch training, a minimum $1,500 grant, travel support, and All-Access passes to the New Orleans Film Festival. The industry panel selects a winner and runner-up in both the documentary and narrative categories for additional funding, while audience members get a voice of their own, awarding a $500 Audience Award in each category.


Pitchers include:

Luisa Dantas (New Orleans, Louisiana) and Tr'Vel Lyons (Los Angeles, California) - Backwards, Sideways, Forward: “If the world is a dumpster fire, what’s your bucket of water?”, asks Tr’Vel Lyons as he builds community in the hills, streets, and classrooms of Los Angeles, New Orleans and beyond.


Adam Forrester and Artemis Fannin (Atlanta, Georgia) - Our Wicked City: A filmmaker returns to his hometown to confront a legacy of corruption and violence.


An-Phuong Ly (Washington, D.C.) - Untitled: In his search for Bigfoot, Steve finds himself on a path towards self-discovery and healing. 


Amy M. Martinez and Chelsea Hernandez (Austin, Texas) - The School of Hope: At the U.S.-Mexico border, a one-room school becomes a lifeline for three asylum-seeking children.


Sienna Pinderhughes and Carlus Henderson (New Orleans, Louisiana) - Shady Side: An Act of Remembrance: Seven cousins gather for a meal on their grandparents' farm before the property is sold.

Concordia

films.short_description: When a mother falls gravely ill, her 19-year-old daughter becomes her primary caregiver. She must navigate what it means to care for someone who cannot easily receive care, and what it costs to keep showing up anyway.
films.description:
Loosely based on the filmmaker’s own experiences, this film explores the tension that arises when a child is forced to parent their own parent. When her mother Suraya falls gravely ill, nineteen-year-old Hiba becomes her primary caregiver, while her older brother Hisham moves through the household largely unburdened. Hiba and Suraya love each other and wound each other in equal measure, locked in a push and pull that neither knows how to break. As Suraya's condition worsens, Hiba must navigate what it means to care for someone who cannot easily receive care, and what it costs her to keep showing up anyway.

A descendant of the Nubian tribes of Sai and Halfa, she draws from her ancestors' oral storytelling traditions to explore what a Sudanese cinematic gaze might look like (and at).

films.name: Danny is My Boyfriend
films.short_description: When Lucy's new boyfriend Danny asks her to dogsit while he’s out of town, it feels like a major milestone. But the illusion shatters when a stranger on the street, Mechi, recognizes the dog… as HER boyfriend Danny’s dog. Fueled by betrayal and questionable judgment, the two launch a mission to get even.
films.description:
This Slamdance favorite is a fully improvised comedy blending madcap adventure with early-2000s Californian vibes.


Made on the most micro of microbudgets, "Danny is My Boyfriend" presents as a straightforward comedy about payback after two hapless strangers realize they’re dating the same guy. Armed with a three-legged dog and some ill-fitting blonde wigs, Lucy and Mechi journey around LA, engaging casting agents, private detectives and various unhinged associates in their sweetly misguided revenge plot. Ultimately, the titular Danny proves a smokescreen for the film’s real interest: an infectious nostalgia for Y2K-era girl hangs. -ST


Director bio:

Lucy and Mechi have been creative collaborators and best friends for seven years. We feel called to the process of scratching at something larger than ourselves, and committed to the complex work of pulling back the veil of illusion that the modern world has erected between us and the depths of our potential to experience the unknowable.

films.description:
A warm, deeply Louisianan portrait of family, farming, and legacy from Queen Sugar author Natalie Baszile and Hyacinth Parker.


Come spend some time in Sondheimer, Louisiana, home to the Nelson family who have run their farm for multiple generations. Determined to continue this legacy of family stewardship, "Harvest" follows four brothers as they navigate changing conditions of their land due to droughts, constant repairs and unreliable opportunities to exceed forward. The story invites you into a year of their entire family, immersing you in their warmth for each other, as well as the realities that they face. -BT

films.short_description: A renowned pianist relocates with her family to the countryside, where she uncovers a life-shattering truth that forces her to confront the complexities of love, trust, and deception.
films.description:
A gripping Cannes thriller starring Léa Seydoux and the grand dame of French cinema, Catherine Deneuve.


Concert pianist Lucy (Léa Seydoux) moves her family to the country, hoping to help her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) recover from burnout. But when police arrive at their door one morning accusing Phillip of an unspeakable crime, their new life is shattered. Lucy must protect their young son while grappling with the possibility that she never truly knew her husband. From Corsage director Marie Kreutzer. A Netflix release.


Director bio:

Marie Kreutzer was born on 25 August 1977 in Graz, Styria, Austria. She is the daughter of the Styrian Green Party politician Ingrid Lechner-Sonnek. Kreutzer studied at Vienna Film Academy with Walter Wippersberg and later worked as a lecturer at the Vienna Film Academy.


One of Kreutzer's most notable films, "Corsage," focuses on themes of female rebellion in a historic setting, tackling contemporary female issues. She collaborated with her cinematographer Judith Kaufmann to convey her version of the story of Empress Elisabeth of Austria.


Her films have been screened at the Berlin International Film Festival, 70th San Sebastián International Film Festival, 2022 Cannes Film Festival, 2022 Toronto International Film Festival, and 2022 New York Film Festival.


On 9 April 2026, it was announced in Paris that "Gentle Monster," the new film by Marie Kreutzer, would officially compete for the 2026 Cannes Palme d’Or. The production won the Cannes Marché du Film Investors Circle Prize in 2025, as reported by Euronewsweek.

films.short_description: In a Southern town where silence has long shrouded history, a native daughter unearths the depths of trauma, loss, resistance, and resilience to reveal one of America’s bloodiest labor massacres - and its enduring legacy across generations.
films.description:
A vital Louisiana story of history, memory, and racial justice, narrated by New Orleans native Wendell Pierce.


In Thibodeauxville, Louisiana, where silence has long obscured a history of racial violence, a native daughter returns home to uncover the truth of the 1887 Thibodaux Massacre, when white vigilantes attacked Black sugarcane workers striking for fair wages and humane working conditions. Through descendants, historians, activists, and community members, “Thibodeauxville” confronts a history whose death toll and details remain contested, revealing how buried violence still reverberates across generations, and how remembering itself can be an act of reckoning and resilience. -RLW

This short documentary follows the sisters behind-the-scenes of their creative collaboration on the award-winning feature film "Take Me Home," revealing how seeking answers in creative ways can lead to surprising outcomes.

Her work has ranged from coming-of-age dramas, to biting punk comedies, to German expressionist thrillers; ultimately driven by a desire to create meaningful stories and artistic experiences that resonate with women and the LGBTQ+ community.

When a fraught young couple who are recently engaged host a reunion with old college friends, their heteronormative lifestyle is thrown into question.


Director bio:

Sophie Barnes is a writer/director and actor from Arkansas. Her work explores themes of relational intimacy, queer identity, and repression in the American South. Sophie holds a Masters of Fine Arts in Film and a Bachelor of Arts in Film from University of Central Arkansas. She loves to make movies with her friends, which she believes is what they were made for.

films.name: Scissors
films.short_description: A slasher with a grudge meets his match when a group of queer friends on a weekend getaway turns his killing spree into a night he never saw coming.
films.description:
A slasher with a grudge meets his match when a group of queer friends on a weekend getaway turns his killing spree into a night he never saw coming.


Director bio:

Hannah Alline is a director and actor, best known for her roles on "Doom Patrol," "The Hunt," "Ozark," Adult Swim’s "Yule Log," "Mayfair Witches," and the NEON film "I Love Boosters." She is also the co-founder and producer of the award-winning Juice Box Films. Her work as both a director and producer has been showcased at Sundance, SXSW, Fantastic Fest, HollyShorts, Cannes, and Palm Springs Shortsfest.

events.name: Beneath the Surface: A Fireside Chat with film critic Angelica Jade Bastién, presented by GILEAD
events.description:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.


Boasting 20k+ followers on Letterboxd and over 9k on Substack, Angelica Jade Bastién (New York Magazine, Vulture) shines a light on how films handle race, madness, gender, and desire. With a Black Southern lens, she deconstructs cinema and culture. Join us for an in-depth conversation about her journey, experience, and "hot takes."

events.name: Doc Shorts: Skin Deep
events.description: What does it mean to live unapologetically in your own skin? Four documentaries about desire, identity, aging, gender, and the choices we make to become more fully ourselves.

films.name: No Angel
films.short_description: A 24-year-old stripper with a degree in neuroscience grapples with her decision to pursue financial freedom over a more traditional career path in an era when financial security feels increasingly out of reach for her generation.
films.description:
A 24-year-old stripper with a degree in neuroscience grapples with her decision to pursue financial freedom over a more traditional career path in an era when financial security feels increasingly out of reach for her generation.


Director bio:

Jaja Meloche is a Canadian filmmaker based in Brooklyn. She holds a BFA from Tisch School of the Arts, New York University. She made her directorial debut in 2023 when her film "Grown" premiered at Palm Springs International Shortest. It was selected as a Vimeo Staff Pick and is featured on Director’s Notes and Director’s Library. "No Angel" is her first documentary short.

films.name: Body (Jism)
films.short_description: When aspiring male models get photographed in Pakistan, they end up pushing the limits of socially-decreed gender roles and taboos.
films.description:
When aspiring male models get photographed in Pakistan, they end up pushing the limits of socially-decreed gender roles and taboos.


Director bio:

Saad Zuberi and Husain Qaizar are Emmy-nominated journalists and filmmakers whose work has appeared on BBC, Al Jazeera, Vice, HBO, Netflix, and Channel 4 and screened at major festivals such as Sundance and True/False. Their films explore human rights, identity, and social justice. Saad is a Cambridge Press fellow and PhD researcher; Husain is a cinephile and yet somehow has never seen Kubrick.

films.name: No Mask (Sin Máscara)
films.short_description: A gay Salvadorian filmmaker confronts his insomnia and traumatic memories from his youth to explore the difficult path toward self-acceptance through recreations of his past with the help of a choreographer and a film crew.
films.description:
A gay Salvadorian filmmaker confronts his insomnia and traumatic memories from his youth to explore the difficult path toward self-acceptance through recreations of his past with the help of a choreographer and a film crew.


Director bio:

Rodrigo Dada is a Salvadoran photographer, director and cinematographer based in Mexico City. He studied Communications in Paris, holds a Master’s in Conceptual Photography from EFTI Madrid, and a degree in Cinematography from the CCC. His work spans photography, visual art, fiction and documentary. He has exhibited internationally, including a solo exhibition at MARTE in El Salvador.

films.name: Forcefield of Love
films.short_description: Doris and Dan's lives are full of dancing, sex, and other intimate pleasures as they defy traditional expectations of how we can embrace life, death, and aging.
films.description:
Doris and Dan's lives are full of dancing, sex, and other intimate pleasures as they defy traditional expectations of how we can embrace life, death, and aging.


Director bio:

Liz and Riley have collaborated on documentary projects since 2012. Their work focuses on people and stories they feel are culturally significant and deserve an in-depth, sensitive look. They are drawn to unlikely protagonists and seek the ways humor and poignancy intertwine as a foundational part of the human condition.

events.name: Narrative Shorts: Love Letters
events.description:
A series of lyrical meditations that bear loving witness to land, memory, and change. Each film lingers long enough to see its subject in full, holding space for beauty, complexity, and contradiction. These offerings of sustained attention become a series of love letters.

films.name: You Do Not Exist
films.short_description: In the stillness of his yard, Booker watches the sky fill and empty with passing planes. As the world moves around him, he lingers, circling a memory whose edges blur with time.
films.description:
In the stillness of his yard, Booker watches the sky fill and empty with passing planes. As the world moves around him, he lingers, circling a memory whose edges blur with time.


Director bio:

Dwayne LeBlanc is a first-generation Caribbean-American filmmaker whose work explores migration, visibility, and dual identities. His films include "Civic," named one of The New Yorker’s Best Movies of 2023; "Now, Hear Me Good;" and "You Do Not Exist," which completes his short-film trilogy. A Filmmaker Magazine “25 New Faces” honoree and MacDowell Fellow, he is developing his debut feature.

films.name: Them That's Not
films.short_description: A sudden prison furlough unexpectedly bonds an estranged father with his emotionally avoidant daughter - a Queer, Deaf poet - at their matriarch’s repass.
films.description:
A Queer, Deaf poet, finds herself at her grandmother’s repass, surrounded by her distant family members who don’t care to know ASL. She resorts to finding solace in hidden, lonely moments that she can steal in the pockets of her grandmother’s generational brownstone. Her visit is complicated by the arrival of her father Samuel, who’s 20 years into a 25-year prison sentence, released for the day on a furlough to say goodbye to his late mother.


Director bio:

Mekhai Lee is a proud graduate of the Drama program at UNCSA. He is the 2022 Director’s Fellow on HBO’s “Succession.” Mekhai directed an original short film, “Them That’s Not,” that premiered at Newfest ‘25 Film Festival, since screening at many film festivals including SXSW and Chicago International Film Festival. He is a directing recipient of the NAACP Cinematic Shorts Competition.

films.name: High Water
films.short_description: While caring for his forgetful mother, a son weathers the tides of change threatening his Gullah Geechee home and way of life in the South Carolina Lowcountry.
films.description:
In the Lowcountry, rising sea levels and increased storm threats continue to disproportionately impact Gullah Geechee communities through further displacement and loss of culture. While caring for his forgetful mother, a son weathers the tides of change threatening his Gullah Geechee home and way of life.


Director bio:

Tyquan D. Morton - a Charleston, South Carolina native - is a literary artist and filmmaker, whose work moves between poetry, multimedia installation and film to explore collective memory, communal intimacy, and the living traditions of the Black American experience.

films.name: Arrudas Boulevard
films.short_description: Aquarium guide Nelson is one of the people affected by the frequent flooding caused by torrential rains and the overflowing of the Arrudas River basins in the city, which is now facing the worst flood in its history.
films.description:
Nilson, a guide at the Municipal Aquarium of Belo Horizonte, Brazil, is one of the people affected by the frequent flooding caused by torrential rains and the overflowing of the Arrudas River basins in the city, which is now facing the worst flood in its history.


Director bio:

Matheus Moura graduated in Cinema and Audiovisual from PUC Minas and specialized in production at EICTV in Cuba. He participated as a Bammer at BAM - Bogotá Audiovisual Market 2023 and was selected for Talents Guadalajara 2025. He produced the feature films "O Recado do Fogo" and "Passaporte Pataxó," both awarded and selected for international labs such as CineQuaNonLab, Ventana Sur, among others.

films.name: Blue Heart
films.short_description: Marianne and Pétion, living in Haiti, await a call from their son who has left in pursuit of the American dream.
films.description:
Marianne and Pétion live in Haiti and wait impatiently for a call from their son in the USA. As silence sets in, their fears and worries grow, revealing the fractures in their own lives. The promise of the American dream now seems to elude them, as the line between hope and reality becomes increasingly blurred.


Director bio:

Samuel Suffren is a Haitian filmmaker and producer. He is making a trilogy of short films inspired by the story of his father, which has been showcased at prestigious festivals worldwide, including Cannes, Locarno, Sundance, and FESPACO. He is developing a feature documentary “Job 1:21,” and his first fiction feature, “Pays poète éternel”.

films.name: Under the Mountain’s Shadow (La Sombra de la Montaña)
films.short_description: An old hermit in the Colombian mountains must decide between returning to care for his ailing mother or remaining bound to the past and the mountain that defines him.
films.description:
An aging hermit, Eloy, lives in seclusion in the Colombian mountains, haunted by his grandfather’s ghost and bound to the land. When park rangers bring news of his dying mother, Eloy faces a choice between returning to his family or remaining in the mountain that defines him.


Director bio:

Estrada is a Venezuelan filmmaker who graduated from the Mel Hoppenheim School of Cinema. His films move between documentary and fiction, weaving elements of magical realism into lived reality. His debut documentary short, "Audio y el Caimán"(2024), has screened at over 20 festivals (inc. Sheffield DocFest and Hot Docs), and has received multiple awards. He is currently developing his first feature film, "El Padrote."

films.name: I Play Rocky
films.short_description: The electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn't just meant to write Rocky—he was meant to be Rocky Balboa.
films.description:
Directed by two-time Academy Award winner Peter Farrelly (“Green Book”), this irresistible underdog story is pure crowd-pleasing movie magic.


Behind the juggernaut success of one of the most beloved sports films in history—celebrating 50 years since its original release—is an equally inspiring underdog story driven by ambition and perseverance. “I Play Rocky” chronicles the electrifying true events of a then-unknown actor named Sylvester Stallone who fought tooth and nail to prove his unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write “Rocky”—he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. An Amazon MGM release.

events.name: Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon & Not Dead Yet (Chưa Chết, Mà)
events.description: Feature Documentary "Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon" preceded by short film "Not Dead Yet (Chưa Chết, Mà)."

films.name: Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon
films.short_description: A young Vietnamese American artist sets out to recover her late grandfather’s lost musical recordings, uncovering hidden family stories and forgotten history that shaped her culture’s past.
films.description:
A musical mystery with the emotional pull of “Searching for Sugarman”—and a fascinating window into a lost chapter of Vietnamese culture.


Vietnamese American filmmaker Khoa Ha sets out to recover the lost music of her grandfather, legendary composer Y Vân, whose songs once defined Saigon’s golden age. Traveling across Vietnam, she uncovers rare recordings, family stories, and a forgotten chapter of Vietnamese music history shaped by war and displacement. Spanning three generations, the film becomes an intimate journey of memory, cultural inheritance, and the enduring power of music.



Director bio:

Khoa is a multifaceted artist whose journey spans continents and cultures. Born in Vietnam, she moved to California in 2011, honing her design and art direction skills at top LA agencies before founding her own studio.


Victor captures the truth that connects all humans. Born in France, raised in LA by filmmakers, he turns intimate stories into work that resonates with any audience.

films.name: Not Dead Yet (Chưa Chết, Mà)
films.short_description: Members of a funeral brass band in Saigon reflect on their intimate proximity to death.
films.description:
Members of a funeral brass band in Saigon reflect on their intimate proximity to death.


Director bio: Horatio Nguyễn is a New York–based filmmaker and photographer. His practice blends fiction and nonfiction storytelling, resulting in hybrid works that fuse the staged in search of lyrical truths. He is first-generation Vietnamese American born in Pascagoula, Mississippi.

events.name: Doc Shorts: The Gay Archive
events.description:
What gets memorialized, who gets erased, and what survives? These three shorts dig into queer history through forgotten stories, archival fragments, and the act of remembering.

films.name: Odd Man In
films.short_description: Odd Man In explores the complex double life of Donald Webster Cory, a mysterious writer who helped ignite the early gay rights movement—and then betrayed it.
films.description:
"Odd Man In" explores the complex double life of Donald Webster Cory, a mysterious writer who helped ignite the early gay rights movement—and then betrayed it.


Director bio:

Matt Nadel is a documentary filmmaker whose work explores queer history, survival, and the contradictions of American life. Shortlisted for an Academy Award, his latest film, "Cashing Out," examines a controversial industry that emerged in the early days of AIDS—and his own unlikely connection to it. Matt’s work has been distributed by the New York Times, The New Yorker, and PBS.

films.name: Bachelors Only
films.short_description: A forgotten 1955 Mardi Gras riot in New Orleans resurfaces through fragments, voices, and historic footage, questioning the writing of history.
films.description:
A forgotten 1955 Mardi Gras riot in New Orleans resurfaces through fragments, voices, and historic footage, questioning the writing of history.


Director bio:

Lasse Lau and Flo Maak have collaborated for over a decade on exhibitions, lectures, workshops, and a book on queer geographies. Their project "Technologies of the Kitchen" links the Compton's Cafeteria riots to J.H. Kellogg, inventor of cornflakes and anti-masturbation devices, tracing how queer bodies are shaped. Mediums span video, embroidery, ceramics, and food, shown from Mexico City to Seoul.

films.name: Maurice and Marvin
films.short_description: A meditation on how one man, facing inconsolable grief, used photography—and Instagram—to cope, to honor his husband, and to create an online community for others mourning their own loved ones.
films.description:
A meditation on how one man, facing inconsolable grief, used photography—and Instagram—to cope, to honor his husband, and to create an online community for others mourning their own loved ones.


Director bio:

David Friend is a journalist, editor, author, curator, and producer. He is a Vanity Fair contributing editor and was LIFE’s director of photography. The doc short "Maurice and Marvin" (2026) is his directorial debut. His executive producing efforts include "MLK/FBI" (Oscar-shortlisted, 2021) and two Emmy-winning films, "Lakota Nation vs. United States" (2024) and "9/11" (2002).

films.name: Other Houses
films.short_description: Immigrant Radka Winslow must choose between the American Dream or living a creative life back in Bulgaria. This film tells the poetic and funny story of Radka’s life-changing summer of choices.
films.description:
A new chapter in the film series from the makers of beloved NOFF Jury Prize winner “Proud Citizen” and “Fort Maria,” with Katerina Stoykova returning in the lead.


What would you give up to make room for the life you want? Bulgarian immigrant Radka Winslow (Katerina Stoykova) has decided to sell her home and return to Bulgaria to pursue poetry full-time. As potential buyers tour her house, Radka’s poems, letters, and conversations transform the process of leaving behind her American Dream into something much more personal. "Other Houses" blurs the lines between reality and fiction, marking another compelling collaboration between directors Southerland, Gentry, and lead Stoykova. -FM



Director bio:

Thomas Southerland and S. Cagney Gentry are southern filmmakers who have collaborated on three films together. "Fort Maria" (2018) screened at NOFF and won the Jury Prize and Best Cinematography award at the Ashland Independent Film Festival and the Best Director award from the BendFilm Festival in 2018.

events.name: Cinema Reset: Time According to Sweet Wreath
events.description:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.


A mythopoetic tale about media, memory, and the constellation of artists & freethinkers in central Alabama known as Sweet Wreath. This expanded cinema performance by Jasper Lee weaves live scoring & spoken word with montages of super8 footage, photographs, drawings, videos, and music from the Sweet Wreath archives. 


Sweet Wreath is a project based in Alabama since 2016 which presents performances and publishes music, maps and books by artists working in the American underground & beyond. Notable releases include Johnny Coley's Mister Sweet Whisper, Silica Gel's Wooden Shoe, & Sun Ra's Magic City: A Cosmo-Mythic Map of Birmingham, among others. More info at www.sweetwreath.com.


Jasper Lee's work with sound & media includes performing in groups (with Johnny Coley, Vernal Scuzz, Silica Gel), making experimental films, and creating multimedia installations. Lee's work with the moving image includes art films and music videos which have screened at festivals internationally. His work with sound includes making instruments, radio art broadcasts, film scores and an array of recorded releases.


Cinema Reset is the NOFF expanded media showcase. Founded in 2011, the showcases groundbreaking projects at the intersections film, art, technology, and performance. We also offer workshops to share unique creative resources with the New Orleans community.


Cinema Reset is curated by Rachel Lin Weaver.

films.name: The Tropic Sun and His Eyes (Soley Twopikal Ak De Je Li)
films.short_description: A despondent young man embarks on a journey to reconnect with his estranged father. Accompanied by an inquisitive street kid, he races against time to share his father's parting words before it's too late.
films.description:
A gorgeous, deeply personal portrait of Haiti and the bonds that tie us to home. From a South Pitch alum, the film premiered at Tribeca earlier this year.


A despondent man journeys by foot through the vibrant streets of Cap-Haïtien to reconnect with his estranged, dying father. Accompanied by a lone street kid and his camcorder, he grapples with memory, vulnerability, belonging, and a  love of place. Shot entirely in Haiti, Elisee Junior St Preux’s "The Tropic Sun and His Eye" weaves these themes into a tender portrait of a son in search of himself within his father and his country. -ZB



Director bio:

Elisee Junior St Preux is a Haitian-American filmmaker and actor born in Miami, Florida. His ultimate mission is to change the stigmatized depiction of Black and Caribbean boys and their fathers with a more loving, vulnerable image. Elisee’s goal is to share stories that reflect the present, honor the past, and reimagine the future.

events.name: Narrative Shorts: Del Mar y el Sol
events.description:
All filmed in Puerto Rico, these three sun-soaked shorts evoke the taste of sea salt and the feeling of sand between your toes, alongside the nostalgia of leaving/coming home, and how place shapes who you are.

films.short_description: Maite, a young graffiti writer in Puerto Rico, faces a life-altering choice: leave the island for a promising career opportunity abroad or stay and navigate the challenges of a nation in crisis.
films.description:
Maite, a young graffiti writer in Puerto Rico, faces a life-altering choice: leave the island for a promising career opportunity abroad or stay and navigate the challenges of a nation in crisis.


Director bio:

Camila Rodríguez López is a Puerto Rican-Venezuelan filmmaker, writer, and cultural organizer from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Her work blends fiction, documentary, and community engagement to build cultural archives, expand access to the arts, and tell stories centered on women, migration, inequality, and the enduring legacies of colonialism.

films.name: Falling White Leaves (Caen Hojas Blancas)
films.short_description: A long-estranged father and son reunite for a photographic road trip through the south of Puerto Rico, unaware that their scenic journey will lead them to the unexpected discovery of a new branch in their family.
films.description:
A long-estranged father and son reunite for a photographic road trip through the south of Puerto Rico, unaware that their scenic journey will lead them to the unexpected discovery of a new branch in their family.


Director bio:

Puerto Rican director Alejandro D. Orengo Colón creates intimate dramas rooted in everyday life on the island. His minimalist, documentary-laced approach emphasizes emotional authenticity and human connection. His films have screened internationally, including at San Diego Latino, Philadelphia Latino, and Trinidad + Tobago Film Festival.

films.name: Chulo
films.short_description: Gael visits their family in Puerto Rico at the height of summer, and soon meets Mateo, a handsome local who changes their life forever.
films.description:
While visiting family in Puerto Rico, Gael forms an unexpected connection with a handsome local that reshapes their understanding of love and belonging. Set against the island's breathtaking landscapes, the film is a tender portrait of queer romance, heritage, and the places that define us.


Director bio:

Joshua Hernandez is a filmmaker/actor of Puerto Rican descent, born and raised in Miami, Florida. Their films have screened worldwide and they are a recipient of the 2023-2026 Miami Artist Grant, 2025; 2021 New York Foundation for the Arts Grant; 2026 Out on Film Filmmaker Fund; and 2026 Puerto Rican Film Commission Sponsorship. Joshua can be seen on "The Walking Dead: Dead City" on AMC.

films.name: Loves Company
films.short_description: A faded gameshow personality is rescued after a car crash by his #1 (and only) fan left, a Florida outcast who he believes has trapped him in her creepy, Everglades home. However, she quickly learns he’s not the bubbly, fun personality she knows from TV.
films.description:
A faded gameshow personality is rescued after a car crash by his #1 (and only) fan, a Florida outcast who he believes has trapped him in her creepy Floridian home. Shot in New Orleans and featuring Brian Batt, Jack Plotnick, and Rachel Dratch. 


“Misery” (Rob Reiner, 1990) gets a gloriously campy and darkly comedic makeover that revels in its Southern sensibility. Dratch and Plotnick shine as two parasitic sides of the same fame-rattled coin: a parasocial obsessive and fame hungry cynic, thrown together into the swampy Florida Everglades thanks to booze, fate, and an accidental crime or two. In this version, however, it’s Dratch’s fannish Antoinette who ends up appearing the saner of the two. Never meet your heroes, indeed. -ST


Director bio: Jason Laurits is a New Orleans-based writer/director, as well as an established graphic artist, with his gallery, Paste, in the heart of the French Quarter. With two award-winning shorts already under his belt, "Loves Company" is his first feature film.


Sponsored by:

films.name: La Bola Negra
films.short_description: La Bola Negra tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain and inheritance, across three different eras - 1932, 1937, and 2017
films.description:
From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi—popularly known as Los Javis—La Bola Negra follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret—one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase. The film also stars Miguel Bernardeau (Rafael), Goya winner Lola Dueñas (Teresa), Academy Award® winner Penélope Cruz (Nené), Golden Globe® winner Glenn Close (Isabelle), and Emmy®-nominated Julio Torres (Juan Pablo).



Director bio:

Javier Calvo (Madrid, 1991) and Javier Ambrossi (Madrid, 1984) are directors, screenwriters and producers. They are the creators of "La Mesías" (2023), which premiered in the Official Selection at the San Sebastián Film Festival and selected at the Sundance Film Festival, becoming the most award-winning series in the history of Spanish audiovisual. They also created the acclaimed series "Veneno" (2020), which became a phenomenon in the United States, and "Paquita Salas" (2016–2019), whose three seasons are an absolute flagship of Spanish pop culture.


Sponsored by:

events.name: Heaven Above Rowen + Bleu
events.description: Feature film "Heaven Above Rowen" preceded by short film "Bleu."

films.name: Heaven Above Rowen
films.short_description: Under the influence of experimental smokable medication, Rowen Amadeus Camor (Alice Voena) is a queer cult leader consumed by psychedelic visions. After forming the Church of Avalon through the guidance of Promise (John Cameron Mitchell), a hallucinated deity, Rowen faces a slow mental breakdown as they search for identity and meaning the day before a prophesied religious doomsday.
films.description:
A psychedelic queer fever dream in the tradition of Kenneth Anger and early experimental cinema. 


Traversing the psychedelic wonderings of magnetic cult leader Rowen, the film creates its own language of experimentation by blending tactile digital textures with makeup, projections, and animation to create a pastel-soaked world that completely envelopes the senses and rewrites the rules of our reality. Guided through this fairytale by enigmatic Promise (voiced by John Cameron Mitchell) this is a directorial debut unlike any other. Director Alice Voena bravely and serenely paints a new landscape for exploring identity, gender, religion, and the liminal space where they all meet. -LD



Director bio:

Alice Voena is a trans filmmaker and multifaceted artist based in New York City. Cutting her teeth as John Cameron Mitchell's tour manager, Alice has been an active member of the underground NYC drag scene. Alice's art questions the absurdity of life and focuses on the connection that people hold with identity, mortality, and one's own body. "Heaven Above Rowen" is Alice's first feature film.

films.name: Bleu
films.short_description: What's there to do, when you're no longer bleu? When Pat loses out on their dream role, they find it increasingly hard to break out of character.
films.description:
What's there to do, when you're no longer bleu? When Pat loses out on their dream role, they find it increasingly hard to break out of character.


Director bio:

Haiba Khan's debut short film "I Hate Birthdays!", which she wrote, directed and produced, won the festival prize for best narrative short film at the New York Short Film Festival in 2024. The film was programmed with GIRLSINFILM and is available online. She recently starred in Michelle Uranowitz and Daniel Jaffe’s film, ‘Clarities’, that premiered at Slamdance in 2026.

films.name: Pinball
films.short_description: A contemplative coming of age portrait that follows Yosef, a spirited athlete, in Louisville, Kentucky as he dives into the memories of his journey from Iraq to America and what it means to chase his dreams in the shadow of a war that displaced his family from their homeland.
films.description:
Quietly moving and deeply personal, Pinball finds an unexpected coming-of-age story in the complicated experience of growing up between cultures.


Uprooted from Iraq as a child and raised in Kentucky,19-year-old Yosef confronts the aches of cultural dissonance in his search for home. Alongside his sister Azraa, Yosef reckons with the legacy of displacement as he navigates family expectations and financial pressures. "Pinball" is a resonant and evocative coming-of-age portrait that lays bare the vulnerability of developing a sense of belonging within a diaspora. -AT



Director bio:

Naveen’s feature debut, "Pinball" premiered at True/False. It was named Top 5 of the Fest by Collider and described as “of genuine artistic poise” in the WSJ. He is a fellow of BAVC Media Maker, Firelight Doc Lab, and Film Independent's Project: Involve. Naveen co-founded Hyphen Film Center in Louisville dedicated to the intimacy of the microcinema and its ability to foster community and conversation.

films.name: This is the House: If I Don't See You, I Love You
films.short_description: Ruminating on home as a site of memory, a Ghanaian-American father and daughter duo work through their crowded basement in search of family archives. Through intimate conversation, they reconcile familial distances, caused by immigration, divorce, and loss.
films.description:
Ruminating on home as a site of memory, a Ghanaian-American father and daughter duo work through their crowded basement in search of family archives. Through intimate conversation, they reconcile familial distances, caused by immigration, divorce, and loss.


Director bio:

Claudia Owusu is a writer and filmmaker whose work divulges the nuance of Black girlhood through a personal and collective lens. She is the author of the chapbook, "In These Bones I am Shifting" from Akashic Books. Her work has received support and fellowships from the Blue Mountain Center, the Ohioana Library, the Greater Columbus Art Council, and Blackstar Pitch.

films.name: Zenón and the Rebel Boats
films.short_description: A biographical documentary about the life of fisherman, Carlos "Taso" Zenón who led the fishermen movement in Vieques to halt US Navy war games in the Caribbean Sea.
films.description:
An essential rediscovery of a Puerto Rican revolutionary and environmental hero in this Blackstar Film Festival Jury Winner.


Through never-before-seen archival footage, Juan Carlos Dávila Santiago chronicles the life and activism of Puerto Rican fisherman and revolutionary Carlos “Taso” Zenón, who spent decades organizing and fighting against the US military occupation of the island of Vieques, Puerto Rico. "Zenón and the Rebel Boats" transports the audience to Vieques to witness an unsung hero in a landmark environmental and anti-militarist campaign in the Caribbean. -JDOM



Director bio:

Born and raised in the westside of Puerto Rico, Juan C. Dávila Santiago is a documentary filmmaker, TV producer, and multi-media journalist. For more than 10 years, Dávila Santiago has reported and produced films about the colonial experience in Puerto Rico, focusing on environmental conflicts, social movements, and workers struggles.

Leo Černic (Čino) is a Slovenian-Italian filmmaker who graduated in Film and Television Directing at AGRFT Ljubljana and Animation at CSC Turin. films.name: The Worm
films.short_description: Kieran is convinced a telepathic earthworm is manipulating him into making bad choices in his life. His concerned family decide to stage an intervention. The result? An amusingly bizarre showdown between reason, belief and one very unlucky invertebrate.

films.name: burn, scar
films.short_description: When a prescribed burn set by the Forest Service accidentally ignites the largest wildfire in New Mexican history, two sides of a centuries-old conflict collide.
films.description:
For anyone curious about disaster recovery, government mistrust, and what happens when local knowledge collides with federal power.


When a prescribed burn set by the US Forest Service becomes the largest wildfire in New Mexico history, a community is left to reckon with devastating loss and a century of mistrust. Following families and Forest Service crews through the aftermath of disaster, “burn, scar” asks who gets to shape the future of a place, and how community knowledge collides with federal power, disaster recovery, and a climate rapidly changing the terms of survival. -RLW



Director bio:

Hillary Bachelder is an award-winning documentary director, cinematographer, and editor based in New Mexico. "Represent," her critically-acclaimed first feature, screened in over 60 theaters across the country and broadcast nationally on PBS’ Independent Lens in October 2020.


Film Sponsored by:

films.name: The Debut
films.short_description: A shy woman is unexpectedly cast in a local production of an original musical. Under the spell of the strong-willed and enigmatic director, she loses herself in the role of a community theater production.
films.description:
Jesse Eisenberg follows his Oscar winning directorial debut A Real Pain with this deliriously funny A24 comedy starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti.


Mona Friedman (Julianne Moore) is a shy New Jersey housewife with no acting experience when she unexpectedly lands a small role in a community theater musical. Under the demanding direction of Jerry (Paul Giamatti), Mona throws herself into the part with increasingly obsessive commitment, discovering a new sense of purpose—and losing her grip on where the character ends and she begins. A funny, affectionate satire of community theater and the transformative power of making art. An A24 release.

films.name: Tender Loving Care
films.short_description: Amy, a government child protection worker, moves back with her upbeat best friend Rosie, a social services officer facing daily anger and resentment. Amy's aging parents worry about her happiness while dealing with their own crisis.
films.description:
Mike Leigh’s latest—and possibly final—film is a warm, funny, deeply human drama that has been a festival favorite from Toronto and Telluride to Venice and New York.


After a painful breakup, social worker Amy (Kate O’Flynn, Emmy winner from “Widow’s Bay”) moves in with her longtime friend Rosie (Alice Bailey Johnson), whose own work caring for vulnerable people leaves little room for her personal life. Meanwhile, Amy’s aging parents face a crisis of their own. As their lives intersect with the people they care for, Leigh finds humor, heartbreak, and unexpected tenderness in the everyday act of showing up for one another. A Bleecker Street release.



Director bio:

Mike Leigh (born 20 February 1943) is an English screenwriter, producer, director and former actor with a film, theatre, and television career spanning more than 60 years. His accolades include prizes at the Cannes Film Festival, the Berlin International Film Festival, and the Venice International Film Festival, three BAFTA Awards, and nominations for seven Academy Awards. He also received the BAFTA Fellowship in 2014, and was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in the 1993 Birthday Honours for services to the film industry.


Leigh is known for his lengthy rehearsal and improvisation techniques with actors to build characters and narrative for his films. His purpose is to capture reality and present "emotional, subjective, intuitive, instinctive, vulnerable films."


Leigh received Academy Award nominations for Best Director and Best Original Screenplay for "Secrets & Lies" (1996) and "Vera Drake" (2004). He received further Academy Award nominations for "Topsy-Turvy" (1999), "Happy-Go-Lucky" (2008), and "Another Year" (2010).
