Mars Verrone is an Emmy-nominated filmmaker, musician, and educator from Los Angeles, CA, currently based in Brooklyn, NY. Most recently, Mars directed, produced, edited and composed original music for their short documentary, "Buckskin," about their grandfather Carroll B. Williams, a ground-breaking African-American forester. Mars is a Sundance Documentary Producers Fellow, NBC Original Voices Artist Mentor and Fellow, PGA Create Fellow, Firelight Media Impact Fellow, Brown Girls Doc Mafia Sustainable Artist Fellow, Dear Producer Mentee, and was selected for DOC NYC’S 2024 “40 Under 40” cohort. Their work has been supported by Sundance Institute, Ford Foundation, Field of Vision, and the International Documentary Association, among others.

films.name: Before We Forget
films.short_description: Where do languages go when they die? "Before We Forget" is an experimental meditation on the loss of Creole French in a family and the ways it lives on in their collective memory.
films.description:
Where do languages go when they die? "Before We Forget" is an experimental meditation on the loss of Creole French in a family and the ways it lives on in their collective memory.


Director bio:

Sydney is an American documentary filmmaker and researcher whose work explores identity, memory, and community through intimate and experimental storytelling. With a background in nonprofit advocacy and fundraising, she approaches filmmaking with curiosity, care, and a commitment to meaningful impact.

films.name: Listen
films.short_description: The Navajo language is spoken less frequently across generations. However, its resilience endures in a small Navajo radio station, the director's family, and the people of the Navajo Nation.

The Navajo language is spoken less frequently across generations. However, its resilience endures in a small Navajo radio station, the director's family, and the people of the Navajo Nation.


Director bio:

Malakye Tsosie, who is from the Navajo Nation, aims to tell honest, unapologetic stories that reflect his cultural identity. He wants to join a group of storytellers who honor and connect with people's stories and truths.

films.name: The Custodian
films.short_description: Having spent over fifty years building a collection of team memorabilia, a devoted Washington Commanders fan sees an opportunity to preserve the collection as the team reckons with its racist legacy and redefines its identity. However preserving the past proves complicated.
films.description:
A devoted Washington Commanders fan has spent more than 50 years building a collection of team memorabilia. As the team reckons with its racist legacy and redefines its identity, he sees a final opportunity to preserve the collection. But preserving the past proves complicated. Between giving impromptu tours, writing to team ownership, and facing his wife’s pleas to declutter, he is forced to confront the contradictions in the legacy he holds dear.


Director bio:

Khaula Malik is an Emmy Award-winning filmmaker based in NYC. She most recently co-produced "Girls Slate" and is currently in post on her first feature doc, "The Nobles" which has received support from DOC NYC and the Catapult Rough Cut Retreat. Her work has been supported by Sundance, HBO, Doris Duke Foundation, CAAM, PBS, and others. She served as a programmer for True/False from 2022 to 2024.

films.name: Frogtown
films.short_description: Welcome to Frogtown, a slice-of-life exploration of the weird and wonderful residents of a small town in north Florida and what they believe in - including tall tales of divine goats, invisible dragons, the skunk ape, and a giant talking frog.
films.description:
Welcome to Frogtown, a hybrid slice-of-life exploration of the weird and wonderful residents of a small Southern town and their beliefs, including tall tales of divine goats, invisible dragons, the skunk ape, and a giant talking frog.


Grounded in the lore of the small town of Marianna, Florida, "Frogtown" emphasizes a sense of everyday wonder. The hybrid narrative/doc format allows this curious cast of townspeople to shine, led by a grandmother eager to prove the existence of the “frog king” she remembers from her girlhood. There’s a tinge of melancholy here: must we accept that things become less magical through jaded adult eyes? The answer is that whimsy is always accessible, but it helps if you listen to kids, visit swamps, and maybe even attend a parade. -ST



Director bio:

Costandinos "Costa" Karalis is a first-generation Middle Eastern American filmmaker based out of Atlanta, Georgia. His work explores the gray area where the worlds of the fantastic and the mundane meet, making for absurd and singular visual experiences that have found him acclaim globally.

films.name: A Paradox of Quantum Superposition
films.short_description: When a disheveled woman realizes her cat is missing, it will take a dream of a memory of long-ago dreams to bring her into a better reality.

When a disheveled woman realizes her cat is missing, it will take a dream of a memory of long-ago dreams to bring her into a better reality.


Director bio:

Sandy Parker is an Italian-American screenwriter, director, and script supervisor based in New Orleans. After training in photography and working as a photo assistant and stylist, she found her way into the film industry by doing craft service. She especially enjoys infusing her quirky sense of humor into stories about underdogs who come out on top.

films.name: Show Me the Line
films.short_description: When an Alabama court jeopardizes access to IVF and her own embryos, artist Abbey Crain refuses to surrender her creative power. In this triumphant tour de force, Crain and a group of fertility patients reckon with the threats to their family future, unearthing hope from an unsettled legal landscape.
films.description:
Where the heartbreak of fertility struggles meets the healing power of art. 


When an Alabama Supreme Court decision halts IVF treatments in the state, Abbey Crain leans into her creative practice as she reckons with what losing access to her embryos means for her family’s future. An exploration into the power of the arts as a tool for healing, "Show Me The Line" follows four fertility patients in a raw and necessary depiction of the rhythmical nature of both grief and hope. -JDOM



Director bio:

Kelsey is a filmmaker and artist with deep Alabama roots. Her work includes five seasons of "Monograph," an Emmy award winning doc series. Through her documentary career, Kelsey’s projects have included storytelling icons such as George Saunders, Willie Nelson, and Wanda Jackson. Her work has screened at PBS Film Festival, AFI Docs, and DOC NYC.

films.name: This is Not a Heartbeat
films.short_description: An essayistic exploration of the rise of ultrasound technology in obstetrics medical imaging, revealing how the machine doesn’t just capture reality, it constructs it.

Carin Leong is a Brooklyn-based documentary filmmaker. Her film "Sandcastles," produced by Field of Vision and a Vimeo Staff Pick, premiered at SXSW in 2024 and screened at AFI Fest and HotDocs, among others. Her work has been supported by Aesthetica, DOK Leipzig, and UFO. In 2024, Filmmaker Magazine named her one of the 25 Faces of Independent Film.

films.name: King of the Chitlin Circuit
films.short_description: At 92, Bobby Rush is still on the road — still climbing onstage, still testifying through his music. This intimate documentary allows Rush's story to emerge the way memory actually works: in fragments, echoes, and sudden, gutting clarity.
films.description:
A rare, intimate look at one of the last great blues showmen, still bringing the house down after a lifetime on the road.


At 92, Bobby Rush is still on the road, taking the stage and testifying through his music. Told in fragments, echoes, and moments of sudden clarity, this intimate documentary stays close to Rush, with reflections from his longtime band members. Born in rural Louisiana, Rush rose from Delta juke joints to Grammy stages, sharing bills with blues legends before appearing in "Sinners" and performing at the Academy Awards. Rather than a career retrospective, the film is a portrait of an artist still performing for his life.



Director bio:

Al Warren is a director and actor who lives in California, originally from Mississippi. His directorial debut is "Dogleg" and he has directed over 100 short documentary films for production company Yours Truly. Warren appears in "Dream Scenario," and "The Drama" and stars in the upcoming thriller "Godhead." "King Of The Chitlin Circuit" is Al's first feature documentary as director and editor.

events.description: From the Yucatán to Gaza to the Mississippi River, these five films explore what it means to hold onto home when the ground beneath you is shifting.

films.short_description: In a quiet town deep in the Yucatán Peninsula, Virginio confronts the mythical Xtabay—a Mayan mythic figure who lures souls to their fate—as well as the shadows of his father and ancestors lost to alcoholism and despair.

Director bio: Chica Barbosa is a Mexican-Brazilian filmmaker based in LA, working across narrative, documentary, and experimental film. Her work explores identity, displacement, and postcolonial experience through lyrical, symbolic storytelling. She's screened at IDFA, Sheffield Doc/Fest, DOC NYC, and is developing her first narrative feature, a Mexico-US co-production.

films.name: Free Fish
films.short_description: Two brothers in Gaza are bound by the sea but divided by displacement.  Once a horizon of freedom, the sea is now occupied and weaponized. Yet fishing remains both survival and defiance, a fragile thread of dignity against erasure.

Bisan is a 26-year-old Palestinian filmmaker and director based in Gaza, who has documented daily life there for five years. She created “Hakawatiya,” a TV and social media program exploring Gaza’s communities, culture and heritage. She has worked with Roya TV, Al Jazeera and Al Arabiya, producing documentaries during the genocide. Her work has received an Emmy Award and a Peabody Award.

films.name: Hummingbird

films.name: La Mar
films.short_description: Once a vibrant fishing village on the coast of Tabasco, Mexico, the ocean is swallowing El Bosque. As tides rise and homes collapse, one woman leads a relentless fight to secure a new future for her community, even if it means leaving behind the only home they’ve ever known.
films.description:
The ocean is swallowing El Bosque. Once a vibrant fishing village on the coast of Tabasco, Mexico, it now sits in ruins. As tides rise and homes collapse, one woman leads a relentless fight to secure a new future for her community, even if it means leaving behind the only home they’ve ever known.


Director bio:

Jean Chapiro is a Mexican filmmaker and journalist based in New York. As a director, she has received a Student Academy Award, Student DGA Award, Cannes Lions Young Director Award, and two Ariel nominations. As a producer, she has won two Student BAFTA Awards and was shortlisted for the 98th Academy Awards. She holds an M.S. in Journalism and an MFA in Creative Producing from Columbia University.

films.name: Some Kind of Refuge
films.short_description: Dwellers of the lush and peaceful banks of the Mississippi River live outside the constraints of modern society. Their slowly disappearing way of life depends on resourcefulness, respect for nature, spiritual freedom and resiliency.
films.description:
Dwellers of the breathtakingly lush and peaceful banks of the Mississippi River live outside the constraints of modern society. Their survival and slowly disappearing way of life depends on resourcefulness, a deep respect for nature, and identities that are defined by individuality, spiritual freedom and resiliency.


Director bio:

Alexandra Kern is a filmmaker from New Orleans whose work explores cultural fabric across communities through intimate, character-driven portraits. The rhythms of the American South shape the pacing and sensibility of her films, and her practice also extends into producing work for artists including Dua Lipa, Lil Nas X, and Tyler the Creator.

events.name: Louisiana Shorts: Forgotten Histories
events.description:
What can a place tell you about the people who came before? These two films travel through Louisiana’s schools, coastlines, and family histories to uncover stories of Black education and Filipino settlement that deserve to be remembered.

He also directed the short "The Perfect Day" and produced the horror short "When The Time Comes."

Pablo Larcuen is a Spanish filmmaker based in Los Angeles whose work merges the intimate and the fantastic. Shot on 16mm and 35mm, his short films have been selected and awarded at festivals like Sundance, LAFF, and Sitges, establishing him as an emerging voice in contemporary cinema. He is currently developing several feature projects.

films.short_description: A bouquet of sunflowers travel farther and faster than the hands that picked them.
films.description:

Recipient of the Sundance Institute’s Lynn Auerbach Screenwriting Fellowship, Christian Moldes is a Sundance Development Labs Fellow and Film Independent Episodic Labs Fellow whose feature, Quince Kings, was selected for The Black List’s 2024 Latine List. Born in Puerto Rico to Cuban parents, he tells genre-blending stories centered on Latin American identity.

films.name: Leaf Peeper
films.short_description: A frantic frolic in fall foliage. A stop-motion autumn adventure. A symphony in blaze orange.
films.description:
Autumn adventurers unite! Leaf Peeper takes you on a frantic frolic of Fall foliage until your eyes pop out. Shot on Super 8 in single frames with pixilation, puppet stop motion, frenetic pans, and plenty of plaid, this very short short film packs every second with as many picturesque and picaresque frames as possible, turning leaf peeping into equal parts immersion therapy and extreme sport to capture the sublime bliss of a lovely day out and about.


Director bio: Vito Rowlands is a Belgian filmmaker, scholar, and Associate Professor of Experimental Film and Media at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts. His short films have screened around the world and his first feature is the Metamorphoses-inspired "Ovid, New York" (2024). Vito enjoys all seasons but has a soft spot for Fall.

films.name: Today I Did Not Make Smart Choices

An archival-based family history that tugs at your heart. Winner of the 2026 Tribeca Festival Audience Award for Best Documentary Feature.


Seamlessly spanning borders with nostalgic pulses of Latin American pop culture, Eddie Sánchez excavates his family history by threading intimate interviews with a rich collection of VHS home movies recorded by his parents, Lalo and Beby. This witty and heartfelt feature asks “what it costs to build a home together” as an immigrant family. Sánchez illuminates the quiet compromises of assimilation and the labor of bridging two cultures, driven by an enduring resolve to start fresh in a new place. -AT

films.short_description: Filmmaker Hubert Taylor spent forty years capturing hundreds of hours of footage celebrating Black life in South Georgia, weaving an extraordinary archive into an intimate portrait of his father, the legendary gospel singer Brother Theotis Taylor.
films.description:
Like a visual cousin to “Hale County This Morning, This Evening,” crafted almost entirely of archival footage depicting rural Black life in the South.


Driven by a divine vision, filmmaker Hubert Taylor spent forty years capturing hundreds of hours of footage celebrating Black life in South Georgia. "Windows of Time" weaves this extraordinary archive into an intimate portrait of his father, the legendary gospel singer Brother Theotis Taylor, their tight-knit community, and filmmaking as an act of love and liberation for a prodigal son.

Charlie, her girlfriend Dani, and Charlie’s son Eli evacuate to Texas in the wake of a major hurricane. Stranded far from home with nothing of their own other than the bags they packed for a temporary relocation, Charlie learns her estranged father may be living nearby. As the three travel through a landscape of fading motels and strangers to find him, Charlie is forced to confront the distance between the family she comes from and the one she has a chance to build.

films.name: Sugar Water
films.short_description: When the electricity is shut off one hot summer morning, a mother scrambles to find money to pay the bill. Meanwhile, her eldest daughter's day becomes a quiet journey of determination and imagination as she searches for a way to ease her mother’s burden.
films.description:
When the electricity is shut off one hot summer morning, a mother scrambles to find money to pay the bill while her two daughters—Kya, the eldest, and her asthmatic little sister—face the heat with courage and creativity. Left to care for her sister, Kya’s day becomes a quiet journey of determination and imagination as she searches for a way to ease her mother’s burden. Grounded in the rhythms of every day life in New Orleans, "Sugar Water" is a story about resilience, childhood, and the sweetness that can still be found amid struggle.

films.name: Singing the Shapes: Songs of the Enduring Sacred Harp
films.short_description: One of America's oldest living musical traditions, Sacred Harp singers form a curious subculture where participation gives rise to unexpected harmony across generations, beliefs, and ways of life.
films.description:
World Premiere! A charming celebration of a singular Southern musical tradition where everyone sings and everyone belongs. Followed by a musical workshop and performance.


Strangers gather in churches, community halls, and living rooms to do something remarkably simple: sing together. “Singing the Shapes” enters the world of Sacred Harp, a 180-year-old American musical tradition where there are no performers or audiences, only participants. Loud, raw, and without instruments, its four-part harmonies bring together people of radically different generations, beliefs, and backgrounds. The film explores the unique alchemy of this participatory music, where listening, learning, and contributing together turns dissonance and difference into harmony. -RLW



Director bio:

He began filmmaking through a DIY film collective before starring in independent films including "Pilgrim Song" (SXSW) and "Men Go to Battle "(Tribeca). films.description:
One of the most lauded films of the year—winning praise at Cannes, Telluride, Toronto, and New York Film Festival—this is the feature that puts longtime NOFF favorite Jordan Firstman firmly in the company of America’s most exciting filmmakers.


An A24 film and a Cannes Un Certain Regard selection, Jordan Firstman’s wildly funny and touching feature debut follows a washed-up New York party promoter whose hedonistic life is upended when the 10-year-old son he never knew he had arrives unexpectedly. Starring Firstman in the lead role, alongside Cara Delevingne, Diego Calva, Kirby Howell-Baptiste, and newcomer Reggie Absolom, the film is a sharp, tender, and irreverent story about growing up, unexpected parenthood, and finding family in unconventional places.

films.description:
Made when the filmmaker was just 22, this remarkable debut is for anyone who has ever felt caught between cultures and ideas of home.


A young Korean-American adoptee is forced to confront his sense of otherness when he learns that his birth mother is terminally ill. Caught between his Korean heritage and carefully constructed American life, Si is tasked with an impossible choice: to preserve the life that he’s come to know or come face-to-face with a past he never knew. "Isle Child" offers a bittersweet and intimate coming-of-age exploration of belonging, identity, and reconciling with where we come from. -FM

films.short_description: 16 year-old Caity and her newly sober father, Paul, co-operate their family business: a locally-beloved haunted house. A spooky-season indie with serious dramatic chops, starring Chiara Aurelia of “Cruel Summer” and Morgan Spector of “The Gilded Age.” Tribeca premiere.


Caity runs rampant in the fabricated horrors of her family-run Halloween haunted house, surrounded by the handcrafted ghosts and ghouls of her father’s design and the haunting presence of his hidden addiction. Exploring the last tender moments of a complicated childhood, this heartfelt directorial debut by Lindsay Calleran brings us a story of queer awakening, family pain, and the healing power of honesty nestled in the cozy autumnal world of spooky season. -LD

films.name: The Welcome Table
films.short_description: People from all over the world displaced by climate change and extreme weather are invited to a single table on the levee in New Orleans to meet, talk to each other, and heal.
films.description:
From Oscar-nominated filmmaker Josh Fox (“Gasland”), a global climate-migration story that comes home to New Orleans.


This is a film about the most devastating issue of our time—climate refugees and climate migration. The UN estimates that one out of every three people on the planet will be forced to move due to climate change. The film travels all over the world, documenting the stories of people displaced by climate change—from extreme weather, hurricanes, drought, famine, landslides, and fires. They are then invited to a single table on the levee in New Orleans to meet, talk to each other, and heal. A wall, on its side, can be a table.



Director bio:

Josh Fox is an Academy Award-nominated, Emmy Award-winning director, writer, actor, producer, musician, and journalist, as well as artistic director of the International WOW Company. His latest film, “The Welcome Table,” is a five-continent epic examining how climate change will displace billions of people and cause the largest mass migration in human history. It premiered on HBO in June 2026.

films.name: Dew Drop Inn: Resistance and Resilience
films.short_description: Opening in 1939, The “Drop” helped launch the careers of iconic national and New Orleans artists. It was a critical stop on the Chitlin circuit; providing a safe haven for the Black community during segregation. This is a story of one man and his hotel and music venue that became symbols of resistance and resilience during the struggle for civil rights.
films.description:
From a safe haven on the Chitlin’ Circuit to a landmark of the civil rights era, the Dew Drop Inn is one of New Orleans’ great untold stories.


The story of New Orleans’ Dew Drop Inn is one of resistance, resilience, and Black music. Opened in 1939, the legendary club was a key stop on the Chitlin’ Circuit, providing a safe haven during segregation and launching generations of artists. Owner Frank Painia successfully challenged Jim Crow laws in court, helping pave the way for integration in New Orleans bars and restaurants. After Hurricane Katrina forced the venue to close, New Orleanian Curtis Doucette restored and reopened it in 2024, bringing this iconic piece of New Orleans history back to life.

Film critics have noted Michael crafts impactful stories on the musicians & cultural heritage of his hometown of New Orleans.

films.name: She Keeps Me Young
films.short_description: Michelle is floating through life until a surprising connection with a high schooler challenges her relationship with her overbearing best friend. A bitingly astute and exceptionally hilarious satire.
films.description:
An offbeat dark comedy from multi-film NOFF alum Doron Max Hagay, director of episodes of “Hacks” and “Saturday Night Live.”


Adrift after her husband’s disappearance, Michelle (Blair Beeken) spends her days tethered to her overbearing best friend, Kelly (Katy Fullan), until an unlikely friendship with a teenage girl gives her a renewed sense of possibility. As this new connection threatens their tight-knit (and often toxic) dynamic, "She Keeps Me Young" unfolds as equal parts deadpan, absurd, introspective, and disarmingly hilarious. Featuring supporting performances from the likes of John Early and Patti Harrison, Doron Max Hagay’s feature debut presents a sharp satire of friendship and self-discovery. -FM



Director bio:

Doron Max Hagay is a Brooklyn-based director. He directed an episode for the 4th season of the Emmy-winning series "Hacks" (HBO Max). He directed "Matt Rogers: Have you Heard of Christmas" for Showtime/Paramount+. He also directed the Netflix comedy "Joel Kim Booster: Psychosexual," which was nominated for a 2022 Critics Choice Award for Best Comedy Special. He was previously a segment director for SNL.

films.name: Test
films.short_description: An amateur bodybuilder in rural Ohio must confront a dysfunctional family, substance abuse, and his own emerging sexuality on his quest to become a champion.
films.description:
For fans of “The Wrestler,” “Beach Rats,” and intimate queer dramas about masculinity, desire, and finding your way out.


At the intersection of a defining hyper-masculinity and emerging homosexuality, we meet Eddy, a budding body builder in rural Ohio on the path of becoming a champion. In "Test," we see Eddy Owens reconcile with what one must endure on this path, through addiction, codependency with family, conflicting romantic feelings, and a sense of isolation, all surmounting to achieving his goal of greatness. -BT



Director bio:

Sam McConnell is a writer, director and producer who co-founded McConnell / Hauser in NYC and LA. Their work includes films, commercials and documentaries. He directed the feature documentary “Camp RicStar” (2024) and episodes of the series “The Warehouse Phase” and “Older Hotter Wiser” for Peacock. He produced HBO’s “The Out List” and “The Trans List.” Sam holds a BA and MFA from Columbia University. “Test” is his feature debut.

films.name: A City in the Forest
films.short_description: In Atlanta, a decentralized resistance movement rallies to defend an urban forest from the construction of Cop City, the United States’ largest police training facility.
films.description:
Get an insider’s view into a movement as it’s unfolding, in this story of  environmental activism and grassroots resistance.


Deeply immersed in protest action, "A City in the Forest" follows Atlanta locals as they fight for the environment and against the implementation of ‘Cop City’—the largest police training center in the United States. Utilizing a combination of police body cam video, TV news footage, TikTok clips, and filmed phone video recordings, the film showcases the power of collective organizing in an urgent land struggle. -JDOM



Director bio:

Lev Omelchenko is an Emmy Award Winning film director and cinematographer based in Atlanta, Georgia. He is an Ukrainian-born Brooklyn-raised immigrant. Utilizing both documentary and narrative forms, Lev’s work focuses on telling stories of joyful militancy in the American South.


Nolan Huber is an Emmy Award winning Director, Cinematographer, and Video Journalist who focuses on stories of resistance and liberation movements—particularly in the US South. He is a Ph.D. Candidate who has spent the last five years studying Narrative Paradigm Theory and asking questions about how we can use film, psychology, and social science to disrupt oppression and tell paradigm-shifting stories.

events.name: Write It Bad
events.description:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.


What if, instead of trying to write the right scene, you tried to write the absolute worst one? Join us for our first live screenwriting game! 

Pull a prompt, give it a twist, and we'll set the clock to 10 minutes while you write a glorious mess. Chip away at writer's block by adding a wildly inappropriate character, making the stakes absurd, or completely derailing the scene. Then, with the help of some actors, we’ll bring a few of these “bad” scenes to life onstage and explore what surprisingly useful material might be hidden inside the chaos. Bring a scene from your own project or start from scratch. 


Our only rule: no perfectionism allowed.

films.name: Purple Noon (Plein Soleil)
films.short_description: Tom Ripley is a talented mimic, moocher, forger and all-around criminal improviser; but there's more to Tom Ripley than even he can guess.
films.description:
Alongside our Spotlight screening of “A Talent for Murder,” NOFF revisits three classic Highsmith adaptations. Together, they offer a chance to revisit the cinematic legacy of one of the 20th century’s great psychological thriller writers. Additionally, the screenings of “Strangers on a Train” and “Purple Noon” come with a special introduction that dives into the science and psychology behind the characters and audience response to these thrillers. Supported by Science on Screen, an initiative of the Coolidge Corner Theatre, with major support from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation.



René Clément’s sun-drenched 1960 thriller stars Alain Delon as Tom Ripley, a charming American drifter who travels to Italy with the increasingly dangerous goal of assuming the identity of his wealthy friend. The first major screen adaptation of Patricia Highsmith’s “The Talented Mr. Ripley,” it predates the beloved 1999 American version starring Matt Damon by decades. Stylish, suspenseful, and undeniably seductive, “Purple Noon” also made Delon an international star.

films.name: Thibodeauxville - The Story of the Thibodaux Massacre: Race, Riot, and Resilience
films.short_description: In a Southern town where silence has long shrouded history, a native daughter unearths the depths of trauma, loss, resistance, and resilience to reveal one of America’s bloodiest labor massacres - and its enduring legacy across generations.
films.description:
A vital Louisiana story of history, memory, and racial justice, narrated by New Orleans native Wendell Pierce.


In Thibodeauxville, Louisiana, where silence has long obscured a history of racial violence, a native daughter returns home to uncover the truth of the 1887 Thibodaux Massacre, when white vigilantes attacked Black sugarcane workers striking for fair wages and humane working conditions. Through descendants, historians, activists, and community members, “Thibodeauxville” confronts a history whose death toll and details remain contested, revealing how buried violence still reverberates across generations, and how remembering itself can be an act of reckoning and resilience. -RLW

Director bio:

Jenny Jokela, b. 1990 is a Finnish animation director and artist based in Edinburgh, UK. She earned an MA in Animation from the Royal College of Art, London, in 2017. Her films have received multiple awards, including the Annecy Cristal for Best Graduation Film in 2018 for 'Barbeque' (2017).

films.name: Ball Face
films.short_description: Life throws curveballs, how you react decides if you make it through. An elementary school, girl terrified of sports, survives a chaotic ball game. By the end of the game, she’s completely transformed.

Laurence Thérien is a Montréal-based director, designer, and animator with a focus on materiality and claymation. She completed a Master’s in Animation at the Royal College of Art (2025), where she directed her graduate film, "Ball Face." Laurence has collaborated as a creative director with the National Film Board of Canada (NFB) and the Festival International du Film sur l’Art (FIFA).

films.short_description: With wit and humor, "My Black Is Cracking" follows Danni's reluctant first trip to a dermatologist — and the stigma she has to crack open in herself before she can care for her skin without shame.

Director bio:

Bianca Lambert is a filmmaker, journalist, and creative producer whose work explores storytelling, beauty, and Black women's experiences. Her short "Super High: A Period Piece" has won six awards and screened at Slamdance, Atlanta, and Chicago Film Festivals. Her second short, "My Black Is Cracking," is on the festival circuit this year. Her writing has appeared in ESSENCE, PEOPLE, and HuffPost.

Leto Stojanovic Meade is a UK animation director whose internationally acclaimed films have won awards at Oscar-, BAFTA-, and BIFA-qualifying festivals.


Jonathan Rockefeller is a writer, director, and producer of stage and screen whose honors include two New York Times Critics’ Picks and multiple Drama Desk and BroadwayWorld Awards, including Best Direction, Best New Play, and Best New Musical.

Playdoh Kolo is a New Orleans-based puppeteer, filmmaker, and interdisciplinary artist whose work combines puppetry, found objects, performance, and film. Their films explore surreal and ritualistic worlds through practical effects and handcrafted imagery, drawing on traditions of experimental theater and puppetry.

films.name: Paradaïz
films.short_description: Welcome to a place where the houses have holes, tomatoes are ticking time bombs and snails wander the streets in search of a safe space. Absurdist animation, archival images and slippery childhood memories combine to explore the real meaning of home.
films.description:
Welcome to a place where the houses have holes, tomatoes are ticking time bombs and snails wander the streets in search of a safe space. Sarajevo-born artist Matea Radic uses absurdist animation, archival images and her own slippery childhood memories to explore the real meaning of home.


Director bio:

Matea Radic is a multidisciplinary artist born in Sarajevo and based in Winnipeg, Canada. She fled her birthplace as a child in the summer of 1992 and has been interested in the concept of home and attachment ever since, infusing her art with a signature mix of nostalgia and dark humor.

films.name: With Tapes and Toasts in the Car (Im Auto Tapes und Butterbrot)
films.short_description: In the face of her body fading into stardust, Shari realizes what truly matters to her.

In the face of her body fading into stardust, Shari realizes what truly matters to her.


Director bio:

Kiana Naghshineh is a German-Iranian director from Mannheim. During her studies at the Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg, she created several award-winning films and was nominated for the Student Academy Award, the Student BAFTA, and the Annie Award. As a freelancer, she works as an animation director and designer.

films.name: Tell Me When You Get Home
films.short_description: During a family party, fifteen year-old Honest Cardamom encounters the spirit of an ancestor, reconnecting the teen to her own origin story.
films.description:
Fifteen-year-old Honest Cardamom hasn’t seen her mother since she was four, but at a crowded family party, she begins to feel her presence in ways she can’t explain. When Honest senses the presence of her mother, she finds the courage to ask her uncle about the woman she barely remembers and, in doing so, begins to uncover pieces of herself.


Director bio:

Tshay is a filmmaker and artist from Amityville, NY. She is a writer, director, producer, shooter, and editor whose work is an expansive case for optimism, play, and interiority. Working in close collaboration with loved ones, Tshay creates films across documentary, fiction and hybrid forms.

films.name: The Peril at Pincer Point
films.short_description: On a quest to prove his competency, an inept sound recordist finds himself entangled in a nautical prophecy on the spectral island of Pincer Point.
films.description:
A spooky, surreal comedy where John Carpenter’s 1980 classic “The Fog” meets “Widow’s Bay.” Winner of the NEON Auteur Award at SXSW.


A layabout sound designer desperate to prove himself, Jim is working on a new horror flick from the tyrannical yet lauded b-movie director P.W. Griffin. Sent to the remote island where the film was shot to capture a sound powerful enough to elevate the film's finale, eerie local fables surface about missing youth and a ghostly sea captain recruiting a spectral crew. As Jim entangles himself further into the scenery, and prophecy, he can’t help but ponder the truth of the legend, and if recording it might just cost him more than his career. 


Director bio:

Noah Stratton-Twine is a writer, director, editor, and composer whose work blends sharp character-driven storytelling with a resourceful do-it-yourself ethos. Jake Kuhn is a writer, producer, director, and recent alumnus of the National Film and Television School. Together they directed the crustaceous comedy "The Peril at Pincer Point," which won the NEON Auteur Award at SXSW 2026.

films.name: The Haunting of Pennhurst
films.short_description: For over 70 years, Pennhurst State School & Hospital was called a place of care. What happened inside killed over half its population. After closing in 1987, it left behind unmarked graves and an unresolved history. Today, on those same grounds, disabled performers prepare to scare visitors at the Pennhurst Asylum haunted attraction.
films.description:
Haunted-house thrills meet disability and the reclamation of a painful history. A Tribeca selection for Halloween fans, horror lovers, and disability advocates.


Do you believe in haunted gravesites? There is one filled with unmarked graves at Pennhurst State School and Hospital, which was finally shut down in 1987. Within it are unsolved cases of abuse and torture. These days, the people of Spring City, Pennsylvania, come to these haunted grounds to see the performers who have created an annual halloween spectacle. Many of these performers live with some of the same disabilities of those whose lives ended in this hospital. So as monsters, ghouls and zombies, they are able to reclaim and reap the profits, but not without confronting ideas around what it means to be a spectacle for entertainment, and how to do so on your own terms. -BT



Director bio:

Stenberg, Attie and Poljak are a film directing team based in Baltimore, Maryland and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Between them they have completed three features, numerous shorts and a dissertation that no one will EVER read.

Director bio:

Matt Nadel is a documentary filmmaker whose work explores queer history, survival, and the contradictions of American life. Shortlisted for an Academy Award, his latest film, "Cashing Out," examines a controversial industry that emerged in the early days of AIDS—and his own unlikely connection to it. Matt’s work has been distributed by the New York Times, The New Yorker, and PBS.

Director bio:

Lasse Lau and Flo Maak have collaborated for over a decade on exhibitions, lectures, workshops, and a book on queer geographies. Their project "Technologies of the Kitchen" links the Compton's Cafeteria riots to J.H. Kellogg, inventor of cornflakes and anti-masturbation devices, tracing how queer bodies are shaped. Mediums span video, embroidery, ceramics, and food, shown from Mexico City to Seoul.

films.short_description: A meditation on how one man, facing inconsolable grief, used photography—and Instagram—to cope, to honor his husband, and to create an online community for others mourning their own loved ones.

Director bio:

David Friend is a journalist, editor, author, curator, and producer. He is a Vanity Fair contributing editor and was LIFE’s director of photography. The doc short "Maurice and Marvin" (2026) is his directorial debut. His executive producing efforts include "MLK/FBI" (Oscar-shortlisted, 2021) and two Emmy-winning films, "Lakota Nation vs. United States" (2024) and "9/11" (2002).

Bernadette J. Gonzales grew up in a small town in Colorado and helped her Junior College create a Media Program. She was one of the first five students through it. She moved to New Orleans and has found a career as a Production Coordinator and Supervisor for the past 19 years in IATSE.

films.name: Wild Horse Nine
films.short_description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
films.description:
From Oscar-winning director Martin McDonagh (“In Bruges” and “The Banshees of Inisherin”) comes this festival favorite that earned a 14-minute standing ovation at Venice.


Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways. A Searchlight Pictures release. 



Director bio:

Martin Faranan McDonagh (born 26 March 1970) is a British-born Irish playwright and filmmaker. Known for his absurdist dark humour and provocative style, he has received numerous accolades, including an Academy Award, six BAFTAs, two Golden Globes, and three Laurence Olivier Awards in addition to nominations for five Tony Awards.


His plays, many of which have been produced in the West End and on Broadway, include "The Beauty Queen of Leenane," "The Cripple of Inishmaan" (both 1996), "The Lonesome West" (1997), "The Lieutenant of Inishmore" (2001), "The Pillowman" (2003), "A Behanding in Spokane" (2010), and "Hangmen" (2015). Some theatres have refused McDonagh's plays due to "unpalatable language."


McDonagh won the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film for "Six Shooter" (2004) and has received six other nominations for his work on "In Bruges" (2008), "Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri" (2017), and "The Banshees of Inisherin" (2022). He directed the black comedy film "Seven Psychopaths" (2012) and was executive producer on his brother John Michael's films "The Second Death" (2000) and "The Guard" (2011).

films.name: The Oldest Person in the World
films.short_description: A decade-long global odyssey chronicles the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.
films.description:
A Sundance favorite that turns an obsession with extreme longevity into a funny, moving meditation on what makes a life worth living.


Over the course of a decade, filmmaker Sam Green travels the world meeting the ever-changing record holders for the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of extraordinary longevity becomes something much more personal, as Green confronts the passage of time, mortality, and major changes in his own life. An intimate, often surprising celebration of aging, connection, and the simple wonder of being alive.


Director bio:

Sam Green is a NY-based documentary filmmaker. "The Oldest Person in the World" marks his seventh feature documentary at the Sundance Film Festival. His most recent film, "32 Sounds" (Oscar Shortlist), played opening night of both the 2022 Sundance and SXSW festivals. Sam’s 2004 feature-length film, "The Weather Underground," premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and was nominated for an Academy Award.

films.name: On the Last Day of Christmas
films.short_description: On Christmas Eve, a mother must protect her teenage son when their apartment building is overrun by demonic beings that begin hunting the residents.
films.description:
Baton Rouge goes dark in this terrifying new horror film, shot right here in Louisiana. World Premiere!


Christmas Eve becomes a night of terror when demonic beings invade an apartment building and begin hunting everyone inside. Trapped with her teenage son Curtis, Sadie must battle alongside a group of survivors as their home is transformed into a nightmare. But as the night grows bloodier, they discover these creatures haven’t come by chance. They’re searching for something in particular and they’ll slaughter everyone in the building to find it.



Director bio:

Writer/director Kevin Arbouet is known for his emotionally driven storytelling. "Benji the Dove" was adapted from the beloved Icelandic novel of the same name and "Gridiron Grind" (Fox Studios) was highlighted by IMDB for being a top pick in 2023.

Writer/Director Aisha Evelyna announces herself as a major new voice with this fiercely personal feature debut. SXSW World Premiere.


A chance encounter on the street brings Nola, a struggling sous chef, face to face with her estranged, unhoused father. As she takes him under her care, long-buried wounds resurface threatening to unravel her even more. Aisha Evelyna’s directorial debut "Seahorse" is a meditation on what it means to both offer and receive compassion and forgiveness in a broken world. -ZB



Director bio:

Aisha is a Toronto-based actor and filmmaker committed to realizing stories that centre the marginalized. In 2024, Aisha won a Canadian Screen Awards for Best Lead Performance for her work on the comedy series "The Drop" and was nominated for Best Director. Aisha was named a ‘Screenwriter to Watch’ by the Austin Film Festival and her short film "Alex" (2022) was named a ‘Vimeo Staff Pick.'

films.name: Ephemera
films.short_description: On her last night in Shanghai, Chinese-American actress Asher asks out her hip-hop dance teacher Tori, sparking an electric, city-wide romance that must end by sunrise.
films.description:
For anyone who loves a great meet-cute, a magical night out, and falling in love on screen. Tribeca premiere.


Through a stomach full of butterflies and eyes full of stars, two artists are pulled into a queer romance that unfurls over one night in the streets of Shanghai. Sweet and humorous but unafraid of confronting the bitter bites of life, their romance cushions the blow of loss and an unmoored sense of displacement for one girl and inspires courage and an emboldened sense of self for the other. Come see with a loved one and be transported to one magical night in Shanghai! -LD



Director bio:

Shan Jiang is a writer-director based in Los Angeles. Her debut feature "Ephemera" world premiered in the US Narrative Competition at the 2026 Tribeca Festival. Drawing from experiences between China and the United States, her films explore intimacy, displacement, and the instability of identity across cultures and genres.

events.name: Last Night at the Palm Court

films.name: Last Night at the Palm Court
films.short_description: For 35 years, the Palm Court served traditional New Orleans jazz music and creole cuisine in the French Quarter. In May 2024, the restaurant closed its doors. This film tells the story of the staff, the players, and the music that made the club an international destination for fans of traditional jazz.
films.description:
A love letter to one of New Orleans’ great musical institutions, where traditional jazz, Creole food, and unforgettable characters filled the French Quarter until 2024.


For 35 years, the Palm Court served traditional New Orleans jazz music and creole cuisine in the French Quarter. In May 2024, the restaurant closed its doors. "Last Night at the Palm Court" tells the story of the staff, the players, and the music that made the club an international destination for fans of traditional jazz. Featuring rarely seen archival performances, contemporary interviews, and a soundtrack spanning eighty years of traditional jazz music, the film offers a glimpse into a New Orleans that no longer exists.

films.name: Mexicanamerican
films.short_description: Using present-day interviews and the VHS home movies his family once sent across the border, a filmmaker explores how and why his parents migrated to the US from Mexico, revealing a personal mosaic of one family's struggle to reconcile two cultures between two generations.
films.description:
An archival-based family history that tugs at your heart. Winner of the 2026 Tribeca Festival Audience Award for Best Documentary Feature.


Seamlessly spanning borders with nostalgic pulses of Latin American pop culture, Eddie Sánchez excavates his family history by threading intimate interviews with a rich collection of VHS home movies recorded by his parents, Lalo and Beby. This witty and heartfelt feature asks “what it costs to build a home together” as an immigrant family. Sánchez illuminates the quiet compromises of assimilation and the labor of bridging two cultures, driven by an enduring resolve to start fresh in a new place. -AT



Director bio:

Eddie Sánchez is an award-winning NYC-based filmmaker. Other directing credits include music videos for NYC independent recording artists, the webseries "Screwed," and he is in development for his narrative feature debut as a writer-director. In his previous work as an actor, Eddie appeared in the feature films "When Icarus Fell" and "Princess CYD" (Vanity Fair’s 10 Best Movies of the 2010s).

Auro Angeli Earley (Angie), born to a Mexican-Irish mother from LA and a Tamil father, was raised in a jungle off the Bay of Bengal. With a background in custom fabrication and construction, she is now a New Orleans-based filmmaker recognized for her unique eye, production methods, and multicultural approach to narrative building.

Director bio:

Stevie Cavalier is an actor and filmmaker based in New Orleans. Her most recent short, "Miniature Life," won a Founder’s Circle Award from Louisiana Film Prize and the Joy James Memorial Scholarship from the UpTilt Film Festival. Stevie holds an MFA in Film Production from the University of New Orleans and is passionate about filmmaking in the South.

films.name: Into The Sun
films.short_description: Charlie, along with her girlfriend and son, evacuate to Texas in the wake of a major hurricane. Learning her estranged father may be living nearby, the three travel through a landscape of fading motels and strangers to find him.
films.description:
Charlie, her girlfriend Dani, and Charlie’s son Eli evacuate to Texas in the wake of a major hurricane. Stranded far from home with nothing of their own other than the bags they packed for a temporary relocation, Charlie learns her estranged father may be living nearby. As the three travel through a landscape of fading motels and strangers to find him, Charlie is forced to confront the distance between the family she comes from and the one she has a chance to build.


Director bio:

Monique Champagne is an Academy Award-nominated set decorator and filmmaker whose work is rooted in intimate, emotionally rich storytelling. She has developed a reputation for crafting spaces that feel deeply lived in. Her approach to filmmaking is guided by emotional truth, often exploring themes of displacement, longing, and the fragile beauty found in everyday life.

films.name: Sugar Water
films.short_description: When the electricity is shut off one hot summer morning, a mother scrambles to find money to pay the bill. Meanwhile, her eldest daughter's day becomes a quiet journey of determination and imagination as she searches for a way to ease her mother’s burden.
films.description:
When the electricity is shut off one hot summer morning, a mother scrambles to find money to pay the bill while her two daughters—Kya, the eldest, and her asthmatic little sister—face the heat with courage and creativity. Left to care for her sister, Kya’s day becomes a quiet journey of determination and imagination as she searches for a way to ease her mother’s burden. Grounded in the rhythms of every day life in New Orleans, "Sugar Water" is a story about resilience, childhood, and the sweetness that can still be found amid struggle.


Director bio:

Jordan Joseph is an actor, writer, director, proud New Orleanian and self proclaimed "all-purpose storyteller.” Her work is rooted in reality but sprinkled with light and love—resulting in warm, deeply humanistic narratives. Ultimately, her mission is to showcase the beauty of her heritage through cinema that is as lively, vibrant, and resilient as the city she calls home.

films.short_description: A young Vietnamese American artist sets out to recover her late grandfather’s lost musical recordings, uncovering hidden family stories and forgotten history that shaped her culture’s past.
films.description:
A musical mystery with the emotional pull of “Searching for Sugarman”—and a fascinating window into a lost chapter of Vietnamese culture.


Vietnamese American filmmaker Khoa Ha sets out to recover the lost music of her grandfather, legendary composer Y Vân, whose songs once defined Saigon’s golden age. Traveling across Vietnam, she uncovers rare recordings, family stories, and a forgotten chapter of Vietnamese music history shaped by war and displacement. Spanning three generations, the film becomes an intimate journey of memory, cultural inheritance, and the enduring power of music.



Director bio:

Khoa is a multifaceted artist whose journey spans continents and cultures. Born in Vietnam, she moved to California in 2011, honing her design and art direction skills at top LA agencies before founding her own studio.


Victor captures the truth that connects all humans. Born in France, raised in LA by filmmakers, he turns intimate stories into work that resonates with any audience.

Keva Peters, Jr., is a New Orleans-born, Saint Rose-raised poet, filmmaker, and photographer whose work explores the rich tapestry of the Black Southern experience. A first-generation scholar and graduate of both Dillard University and Florida State University’s film programs, he is pursuing a career in independent filmmaking rooted in Louisiana.

Maxine Sylvina Ayala is a Hispanic Honduran transgender filmmaker, director, and cinematographer from New Orleans, Louisiana and is a recent graduate of Loyola University New Orleans. Miles Caradine is a New Orleans-based writer and director. Born and raised in Oxford, Mississippi, he recently finished his studies at Loyola University New Orleans with a BFA in filmmaking. He continues his work in film production, collaborating on indie shorts, experimental music videos, and student film projects. Caradine has a mean taste in character actresses and bloody guts!

Cameron M. Brown is a filmmaker and producer from Baton Rouge, Louisiana and a recent graduate from Tulane University. Film’s ability to correct and subvert harmful narratives drives Cameron to make bold films that connect with his queer, southern identity. He firmly believes in the power of whimsical, LGBT youth-centered storytelling to bring laughter, warmth, and truth to a sinister world.

films.description:
In New Orleans, three men shaped by fatherless upbringings - including NFL champion Tyrann Mathieu - return to their communities to become the mentors they once needed and help build a stronger future for the city that raised them.


Immediately following the screening, stay in your seat for a live recording of “In The Bayou With Tyrann Mathieu,” the podcast where Tyrann the “Honey Badger” talks sports, life, and culture from a distinctly New Orleans point of view. Recorded live, the episode will dig into the film, the work of Son of a Saint, and what it means to come home and give back to the city that raised you.

Jess Speight is a documentary filmmaker and former University of Michigan football player whose work explores sports, community, and social impact. His passion for filmmaking began while running his nonprofit, TUFF, in college, where hearing the powerful stories of the professional athletes he worked alongside inspired him to bring those stories to a broader audience.

Director bio:

Sabaah Folayan is an award-winning filmmaker whose work combines nuance, optimism and cultural relevance. Her films include "Whose Streets?," which premiered at Sundance; Hulu’s "Look at Me: XXXTENTACION;" and "Ratified," which premiered on PBS in 2025. A 2022 Pew Fellow and 2023 Chicken & Egg Breakthrough Awardee, her work is rooted in behavioral science and social justice.

T.J. Masters is an artist based in Texas. He works as a musician, photographer, and sometime FM radio program host. From radio transmitters and motorcycles to motion picture cameras, he is a self-taught technician and can usually be found building, repairing, or restoring something. He lives with three cats, nine chickens, and an ever-expanding collection of photographic chemicals.

Alistair Little and Stuart Hackshaw are UK based filmmakers who have been collaborating for more than 15 years, working as director and DP in commercials, drama and documentary. Tif “Teddy” Lamson is a self-taught director from Lafayette, LA, whose work is shaped by music and the dreamlike beauty of the Louisiana landscape. As a full-time musician and artist, she directs with a collaborative, artist-first approach that focuses on blending sound and image into emotionally immersive experiences, creating space for stories to emerge with honesty, intuition, and reverence.

Olivia Luz Perillo and Syd Horn are multidisciplinary filmmakers from South Louisiana exploring cultural identity, biographical storytelling, and healing arts through organic visual poetry. films.name: Vindication to Victory
films.short_description: After a wrongful incarceration lands him behind bars for nearly 40 years, Raymond Flanks must adjust to life in the 21st century and chart his future in a world that's remarkably different from the one he remembers.
films.description:
After a wrongful incarceration lands him behind bars for nearly 40 years, Raymond Flanks must adjust to life in the 21st century and chart his future in a world that's remarkably different from the one he remembers.


Raymond Flanks was just 20 years old when he was wrongfully incarcerated at the Louisiana State Penitentiary. He spent nearly four decades in prison for a crime he didn't commit, until suppressed evidence came to light and led to an overturned conviction. Upon his release after almost 40 years, Raymond found that he needed to adjust to life in the 21st century and develop the skills necessary to survive in a world remarkably different from the one he remembered.

His work is driven by the belief that every person’s story—told with honesty, beauty, and empathy—has the power to move hearts and inspire change.

Her work has ranged from coming-of-age dramas, to biting punk comedies, to German expressionist thrillers; ultimately driven by a desire to create meaningful stories and artistic experiences that resonate with women and the LGBTQ+ community.

Sophie Barnes is a writer/director and actor from Arkansas. Her work explores themes of relational intimacy, queer identity, and repression in the American South. Sophie holds a Masters of Fine Arts in Film and a Bachelor of Arts in Film from University of Central Arkansas. She loves to make movies with her friends, which she believes is what they were made for.

Hannah Alline is a director and actor, best known for her roles on "Doom Patrol," "The Hunt," "Ozark," Adult Swim’s "Yule Log," "Mayfair Witches," and the NEON film "I Love Boosters." She is also the co-founder and producer of the award-winning Juice Box Films. Her work as both a director and producer has been showcased at Sundance, SXSW, Fantastic Fest, HollyShorts, Cannes, and Palm Springs Shortsfest.

films.name: Loves Company
films.short_description: A faded gameshow personality is rescued after a car crash by his #1 (and only) fan left, a Florida outcast who he believes has trapped him in her creepy, Everglades home. However, she quickly learns he’s not the bubbly, fun personality she knows from TV.
films.description:
A faded gameshow personality is rescued after a car crash by his #1 (and only) fan, a Florida outcast who he believes has trapped him in her creepy Floridian home. Shot in New Orleans and featuring Brian Batt, Jack Plotnick, and Rachel Dratch. 


“Misery” (Rob Reiner, 1990) gets a gloriously campy and darkly comedic makeover that revels in its Southern sensibility. Dratch and Plotnick shine as two parasitic sides of the same fame-rattled coin: a parasocial obsessive and fame hungry cynic, thrown together into the swampy Florida Everglades thanks to booze, fate, and an accidental crime or two. In this version, however, it’s Dratch’s fannish Antoinette who ends up appearing the saner of the two. Never meet your heroes, indeed. -ST


Director bio: Jason Laurits is a New Orleans-based writer/director, as well as an established graphic artist, with his gallery, Paste, in the heart of the French Quarter. With two award-winning shorts already under his belt, "Loves Company" is his first feature film.

films.name: Maestro
films.short_description: In New Orleans, where music is woven into the city's identity, legendary band director Wilbert Rawlins Jr. has spent more than three decades transforming the lives of children through his marching band. As he fights to rebuild his band after the pandemic while guiding his students through violence and poverty, "Maestro" reveals how one man's unwavering belief in young people can change the course of countless lives.
films.description:
More than a marching-band movie, “Maestro” is a moving New Orleans story about the power of music—and one remarkable man using it to change young lives.


In the historic neighborhood of Algiers, New Orleans, beloved band director Wilbert Rawlins Jr. has spent more than 30 years using music to save lives. At L.B. Landry High School, he leads one of the city's top marching bands while guiding students through the daily realities of gun violence, poverty, and systemic neglect, helping more than a dozen earn college scholarships each year. 


Filmed over multiple years, "Maestro" offers rare, intimate access as Rawlins faces the greatest challenge of his career, rebuilding his band after the pandemic. It's a powerful portrait of one man's fight to lift up a generation of young people through music.

films.short_description: A renegade reporter uncovers a cardboard-laced conspiracy while pursuing a deadly political scandal connected to the local sanitation strike.
films.description:
What could possibly make you cry over cardboard? A proudly DIY, Baton Rouge–made political satire about corruption and conspiracy.


A renegade reporter uncovers a cardboard-laced conspiracy while pursuing a deadly political scandal connected to the local sanitation strike. “Beware the Box Folk” challenges current societal norms and questions where the real solutions lie in a world that constantly suggests progress is coming and yet never seems to arrive. Through a surrealist lens, the filmmakers investigate political conspiracy, capitalism, homelessness, and what lies behind fundamental human intentions.


Director bio:

Nathan S. Hall and Brendan Pyron are a directing team currently based in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.


They've been collaborating for over fifteen years, continuing to explore their surrealist yet deeply human vision within larger and larger film productions.


The duo also co-founded the Baton Rouge Underground Film Festival to inspire and uplift the next generation of genre, auteur filmmakers.

films.short_description: In a house between the mountains, facing a mirrored lake, Emma and her teenage granddaughter Alicia live together. Emma instills her passion for dance and raises Alicia as a mother, but Alicia falls prey to her controlling upbringing. The unexpected arrival of Barbara, Alicia’s mother and Emma’s daughter, accompanied by her caregiver, disrupts the routine of their small world.
films.description:
An enigmatic, dance-driven portrait of three generations of women, set against the wild beauty of southern Argentina—for fans of sumptuous international cinema. 


On the banks of a freshwater Patagonian lake, Alicia and her grandmother fill their days of solitude with a curious study of dance that centers feeling over conventional form. When their serenity is interrupted by the return of Alicia’s mother who suffers an unnamed disease that leaves her non-verbal and childlike, the balance of their duality shifts to a mystic trio. The mysterious landscape of their secluded home begins to unveil its secrets as the three women seek to find balance and trust between each other once again. -LD

Her short films include "Mi reina" (Punta del Este Film Festival), "Hoy empieza otra vez" (Bafici, La mujer y el cine) and "Todas mis Lolas" (Marché du film, Primeiro Plano Brasil). She also co-directed the documentary "Me gusta cuando hablas" (Fidba). "Three Times (Tres tiempos)" is her debut feature film.
